title: Directional End-Zone Possession
objective: Develop players’ ability to maintain possession while moving the football purposefully towards a defined scoring end.
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area with a five-metre scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
One team attacks one end while the opposition attacks the opposite end.
Begin with one football and position players throughout the area.
Tackling is replaced by touch pressure for younger or less experienced groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play by releasing the football to one team near the centre.
The team in possession attempts to move the football into its attacking scoring zone.
Players may kick or handball and may move freely throughout the area.
A point is scored when a player receives a legal disposal inside the attacking scoring zone.
The receiving player must enter the zone after the disposal has been released.
Following a score, the opposition restarts from its defensive scoring line.
A turnover occurs after an interception, dropped mark, out-of-bounds disposal or rule infringement.
Play continues for two- to three-minute rounds before teams change attacking directions.
coachingPoints: Encourage players to look forward before using a sideways or backward option.
Create width around the ball carrier to open central passing lanes.
Lead into space rather than standing beside a defender.
Support behind and beside the football so possession can be retained.
Use the appropriate disposal for the available distance and pressure.
Defenders should protect the scoring zone while applying pressure to the football.
Players must transition immediately when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain awareness of the attacking direction.
Whether the team creates usable width around the football.
Whether players lead forward rather than crowding the ball carrier.
Whether the ball carrier scans before disposing.
Whether defenders recover towards the scoring zone after losing pressure.
Whether both teams react quickly after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Stop play and reposition players across the width of the area.

commonErrors.error: The ball is moved sideways without gaining ground.
commonErrors.correction: Reward forward disposals and forward receiving positions.

commonErrors.error: Players wait inside the scoring zone.
commonErrors.correction: Require receivers to enter the zone after the disposal is released.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the football and leave the scoring zone open.
commonErrors.correction: Coach the deepest defender to protect space behind the press.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate support movement after every disposal.

progressions: Reduce the playing area to increase pressure.
Introduce full legal tackling for appropriate groups.
Require a minimum number of disposals before scoring.
Award two points for a scoring-zone mark from a kick.
Require the attacking team to use both sides of the area before scoring.
regressions: Add a neutral player who always supports the team in possession.
Allow defenders to apply delayed pressure after each restart.
Permit a stationary receiver inside the scoring zone for Under 8 players.
successIndicators: Move the football towards the correct attacking end.
Create forward and lateral options for the ball carrier.
Enter the scoring zone with timing rather than waiting inside it.
Recover their defensive position immediately after turnovers.
matchApplication: The game introduces the basic tactical requirement of Australian football: win possession, spread from the contest, move the football towards goal and defend space when possession is lost.

title: Support Triangle Possession
objective: Develop players’ ability to form effective support triangles around the ball carrier and maintain multiple disposal options.
setup:
Mark a square playing area.
Place one two-metre scoring gate on three sides of the square.
Divide players into two teams.
One team begins in possession.
A team scores by completing a disposal through any available gate to a teammate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team moves the football inside the square.
At least two teammates must create different support angles around the ball carrier.
A point is scored when a player disposes through a gate to a teammate positioned outside the square.
The outside receiver immediately returns the football into the playing area.
The same gate cannot be used for consecutive scores.
Defenders attempt to intercept, force an error or touch the football.
Possession changes after a turnover or when the football leaves the area without passing through a gate.
Teams play two-minute rounds and attempt to record the highest score.
coachingPoints: Position one support player ahead of the ball and another behind or beside it.
Avoid placing all options on the same line.
Move early so the ball carrier can identify options before pressure arrives.
Maintain enough distance to prevent one defender covering multiple players.
Re-form the support triangle immediately after each disposal.
Communicate whether the option is forward, lateral or behind.
Defenders should close the most dangerous option while pressuring the ball carrier.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier regularly has at least two visible options.
Whether support players occupy different angles and depths.
Whether players move after disposing.
Whether teammates communicate early.
Whether defenders can cover several attackers because spacing is too narrow.
Whether the possession team scans for a new gate after scoring.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand directly behind defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Lead laterally until the ball carrier has a clear sightline.

commonErrors.error: All support players move forward.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one player to remain behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Players follow their disposal too closely.
commonErrors.correction: Require players to clear five metres before offering again.

commonErrors.error: The same gate is repeatedly targeted.
commonErrors.correction: Enforce the alternate-gate rule and reward early scanning.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers hold the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Introduce a three-second disposal count.

progressions: Require a kick through selected gates and a handball through others.
Allow full tackling for appropriate players.
Award bonus points when all team members touch the football before a score.
regressions: Increase the size of the square.
successIndicators: Create support on more than one side of the ball carrier.
Identify an available gate before receiving.
Retain possession despite changing defensive pressure.
matchApplication: Support triangles provide the ball carrier with forward, lateral and release options during contested possession, defensive exits and open-field ball movement.

title: Timed Scoring-Zone Entry
objective: Develop players’ ability to create and use space inside a scoring zone through correctly timed leads and purposeful forward entries.
setup:
Create a directional field with an eight-metre scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
Each team attacks one scoring zone.
No player may remain inside a scoring zone for longer than three seconds without leaving and re-entering.
A mark inside the scoring zone scores two points; a clean handball receive scores one point.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football near the centre.
The team in possession attempts to move the football into its attacking scoring zone.
Attackers may enter the scoring zone to lead but must leave after three seconds if they do not receive.
The football must enter the zone through a kick or handball to a moving receiver.
A clean kick-to-mark scores two points.
A clean handball receive scores one point.
A turnover immediately changes the attacking direction.
The team that lost possession must recover and protect the opposite scoring zone.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Keep the scoring zone open until the ball carrier is ready to enter.
Lead into available space rather than towards the football.
Use change of pace to separate from a defender.
Ball carriers should lower their eyes and identify the best entry option.
Do not automatically kick long when a shorter lead is available.
Supporting players should remain outside the zone to provide a release option.
Defenders should protect the most dangerous space rather than following every movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers vacate the scoring zone before leading.
Whether leads begin when the ball carrier is able to dispose.
Whether entry disposals favour the receiver’s movement.
Whether players select handball or kick appropriately.
Whether defenders recover to the scoring side after turnovers.
Whether the possession team retains support outside the zone.

commonErrors.error: Attackers stand inside the scoring zone.
commonErrors.correction: Enforce the three-second rule and require clearing leads.

commonErrors.error: Players lead too early.
commonErrors.correction: Cue the lead when the ball carrier raises their eyes.

commonErrors.error: Entry kicks are placed directly on the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Kick to the receiver’s advantage side.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers ignore shorter options.
commonErrors.correction: Reward controlled entries rather than distance.

commonErrors.error: Supporting players enter the zone together.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one player outside as the release option.

progressions: Award three points for a mark created by a double lead.
Require one possession switch before entry.
Apply a ten-second limit from possession gain to scoring attempt.
Add an intercept defender inside the zone.
regressions: Remove the three-second restriction for younger players.
successIndicators: Time leads with the ball carrier’s readiness.
Direct disposals into the receiver’s path.
Select the best available entry method.
matchApplication: The game replicates forward-entry situations where forwards must create space, time their leads and provide the ball carrier with clear scoring options.

title: Turnover Reaction Race
objective: Develop immediate team transition from attack to defence and defence to attack following a turnover.
setup:
Create a directional field with a five-metre scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Place a turnover line across the centre of the playing area.
Teams score by completing a disposal to a teammate inside the attacking zone.
The first team to reorganise after a turnover receives a potential bonus point.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team attacking its scoring end.
A turnover occurs after an interception, error, out-of-bounds disposal or coach’s whistle.
The new possession team immediately attacks the opposite end.
The team that lost possession must send at least two players behind the centre turnover line before it can regain possession.
The attacking team receives one point for a scoring-zone receive.
It receives a bonus point if it scores before two defenders recover behind the turnover line.
If the defending team forces a slow entry and regains possession, it receives one defensive point.
Play continues continuously for two- to three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: React to the turnover before appealing, stopping or showing frustration.
The nearest player applies pressure to the new ball carrier.
The next defenders sprint to protect central and deep space.
The new possession team spreads immediately to create a counterattacking option.
The first disposal after the turnover should move the football away from pressure.
Communicate whether the team is attacking, pressing or recovering.
Maintain running support after the initial transition disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
The speed of reaction after possession changes.
Whether the nearest defender applies immediate pressure.
Whether deeper defenders protect the scoring zone.
Whether attackers create width during counterattack.
Whether players continue running after the first transition disposal.
Whether communication clearly changes from attack to defence.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after losing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Make turnover reaction the first scoring criterion.

commonErrors.error: Every defender chases the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign nearest pressure, second support and deepest protection roles.

commonErrors.error: The new possession team remains narrow.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate width outside the turnover area.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal is rushed forward.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage a controlled release away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Players jog through defensive recovery.
commonErrors.correction: Use short rounds and reward full-speed reaction.

progressions: Award extra points for scoring within eight seconds.
Begin selected turnovers with a coach call rather than an error.
Add a second football during advanced tactical rounds.
regressions: Allow three seconds of protected possession after a turnover.
Require only one defender to recover behind the line.
successIndicators: Apply pressure with the nearest available defender.
Protect dangerous central and deep space.
Spread rapidly when possession is won.
Complete a controlled first disposal after turnover.
matchApplication: The game replicates the critical seconds after an AFL turnover, when teams must rapidly counterattack or prevent the opposition from using an unstructured field.

title: Width or Corridor Choice
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when to attack through the corridor and when to use width to retain possession.
setup:
Divide the field lengthways into one central corridor and two wider outside lanes.
Place a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
A normal scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score created through the corridor earns three points.
A score created after transferring from one outside lane to the other earns two points.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play near the centre.
The possession team attacks its scoring end.
Players may use any lane but must assess the pressure before selecting the next disposal.
A direct corridor chain that results in a score earns three points.
A full-width switch followed by a score earns two points.
Any other scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A turnover changes the attacking direction immediately.
Defenders may protect the corridor, press wide or adjust according to the attacking shape.
Teams review their scoring choices after each three-minute round.
coachingPoints: Scan the corridor before automatically moving wide.
Use the corridor when there is clear space, numerical support or a strong marking option.
Use width when the corridor is blocked or heavily outnumbered.
Switch the football with speed so the defence cannot reset.
Maintain support behind the football during higher-risk corridor attacks.
Avoid using width without purpose.
Defenders should protect the corridor while remaining able to pressure wide possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan all three lanes before disposing.
Whether corridor entries are based on advantage rather than forced scoring.
Whether width creates a genuine switch or merely delays play.
Whether teammates support behind higher-risk disposals.
Whether defenders protect central space without conceding easy width.
Whether players recognise changing numbers around the football.

commonErrors.error: Players force the corridor for bonus points.
commonErrors.correction: Remove the bonus after consecutive forced turnovers.

commonErrors.error: The team stays wide despite open central space.
commonErrors.correction: Freeze play and identify the unguarded corridor option.

commonErrors.error: Switches are slow and predictable.
commonErrors.correction: Require the football to move across the ground within three disposals.

commonErrors.error: No support remains behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one player as the release and turnover-protection option.

commonErrors.error: Defenders completely abandon outside lanes.
commonErrors.correction: Coach staggered positioning rather than corridor crowding.

progressions: Award defensive points for intercepting corridor entries.
Require a kick to complete a lane change.
Add a scoring multiplier during the final minute.
regressions: Use passive defenders during the first round.
Add a neutral player in the central lane.
Pause after possession gains to allow scanning.
successIndicators: Identify both central and wide options.
Select the lane that best matches the available space and numbers.
Move the football quickly during switches.
Adjust defensive shape without losing pressure.
matchApplication: The game develops the tactical judgement required to balance fast corridor attack against safer wide ball movement during defensive exits, transition and forward entries.

title: Plus-One Advantage Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify, create and use an extra player during attacking ball movement.
setup:
Create a directional playing area with one scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
Add one neutral player who always supports the team in possession.
The neutral player may move anywhere inside the area.
Teams score through a clean receive inside the attacking zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play with one team.
The neutral player joins the possession team, creating a numerical advantage.
The attacking team attempts to move the football into its scoring zone.
Players are encouraged to draw a defender before releasing to the spare player.
The neutral player cannot score but may deliver the final disposal.
After a turnover, the neutral player immediately supports the new possession team.
A normal score earns one point.
A score created after the neutral player receives in open space earns two points.
Rotate the neutral player every two minutes.
coachingPoints: Identify the spare player before receiving.
Draw a defender before releasing the football.
Maintain enough width for the extra player to remain usable.
Use overlap run rather than standing as the spare.
Move the football before defenders can transfer responsibility.
The neutral player should communicate and reposition continuously.
Defenders should delay the attack and protect the scoring zone until numbers recover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise where the numerical advantage exists.
Whether the ball carrier draws pressure before disposing.
Whether the neutral player remains active.
Whether attackers create enough width for the spare to be used.
Whether defenders communicate switches and delay the attack.
Whether teams use the advantage before it disappears.

commonErrors.error: Players dispose before drawing a defender.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage one or two controlled steps towards pressure before release.

commonErrors.error: The neutral player follows the football too closely.
commonErrors.correction: Position the neutral player outside the immediate contest.

commonErrors.error: Attackers remain in one line.
commonErrors.correction: Create staggered depth around the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: The spare player is ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Award bonus points only when the spare contributes.

commonErrors.error: Defenders overcommit to the ball.
commonErrors.correction: Coach delay, protect and transfer responsibility.

progressions: Allow the neutral player only one touch or immediate disposal.
Introduce a second neutral player with different movement restrictions.
Remove the neutral bib and require teams to identify the spare naturally.
Award a defensive point for forcing the attack backwards.
regressions: Give the neutral player protected possession.
Allow the neutral player to score.
Pause after turnovers so players can identify the new advantage.
successIndicators: Use the numerical advantage to gain territory.
Delay opposition attacks when defending outnumbered.
matchApplication: The game develops the ability to exploit overlap, loose players and outnumber situations that occur after turnovers, defensive exits and running support chains.

title: Three-Second Pressure Game
objective: Develop fast, composed disposal decisions when the ball carrier has limited time and immediate defensive pressure.
setup:
Create a directional playing area with two scoring gates at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
The ball carrier must legally dispose of the football within three seconds.
The coach counts aloud when required.
Teams score by moving the football through either attacking gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
Each ball carrier has three seconds to kick or handball.
A player who exceeds the count concedes a turnover.
Defenders apply controlled match-like pressure.
A team scores one point by completing a disposal through an attacking gate.
A score within six disposals earns a bonus point.
After a turnover, the three-second rule immediately applies to the new team.
Teams play high-intensity ninety-second rounds with recovery between rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving rather than after gaining possession.
Support players must move early and communicate clearly.
Take the first effective option rather than searching for the perfect option.
Protect the football while preparing the disposal.
Maintain disposal technique despite the time restriction.
Defenders should close space under control rather than overrun the contest.
Players must reset their decision process immediately after turnovers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan before the football arrives.
Whether support options appear early enough.
Whether ball carriers maintain disposal technique.
Whether players rush into low-percentage options.
Whether defenders arrive balanced and able to tackle.
Whether the game remains composed despite the time pressure.

commonErrors.error: Players begin scanning only after receiving.
commonErrors.correction: Ask players to call their intended option before possession.

commonErrors.error: Disposals become technically poor.
commonErrors.correction: Increase the limit to four seconds before rebuilding speed.

commonErrors.error: Support players react too late.
commonErrors.correction: Require movement as the previous disposal is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Defenders overrun the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Coach controlled closing steps and balanced body position.

commonErrors.error: Players use the nearest option regardless of danger.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the first effective option, not simply the first visible option.

progressions: Reduce the disposal limit to two seconds.
Require alternating kick and handball disposals.
Award defensive points for forced rushed disposals.
Introduce scoreboard pressure during the final round.
regressions: Increase the disposal limit to five seconds.
Stop the count after a clean mark.
successIndicators: Select an effective option within the time limit.
matchApplication: The game replicates contested match situations where players have minimal time to assess options and execute before pressure arrives.

title: Multi-Method Scoring Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to select between several scoring methods according to space, pressure, numbers and match risk.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Add two scoring gates along each sideline.
Divide players into two teams.
Display the available scoring methods and point values.
End-zone mark: three points.
End-zone handball receive: two points.
Disposal through a side gate: one point.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams attack their nominated scoring end.
Players may choose any available scoring method.
An end-zone mark earns three points.
A handball receive in the end zone earns two points.
A completed disposal through a side gate earns one point and possession is retained.
After a side-gate score, the team may continue attacking.
A turnover changes the attacking direction.
The coach may announce changing scoreboard situations between rounds.
Teams must explain their preferred scoring strategy during short breaks.
coachingPoints: Assess the defensive shape before selecting a scoring method.
Take the highest-value option when it is genuinely available.
Use lower-value scores to retain possession or draw defenders away.
Avoid forcing a three-point option into heavy pressure.
Move defenders by threatening several scoring areas.
Defenders must prioritise the most dangerous option while communicating secondary threats.
Adjust strategy according to score and time remaining.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the value and risk of each scoring method.
Whether teams create more than one scoring threat.
Whether high-value attempts are selected appropriately.
Whether players use low-value options to manipulate the defence.
Whether defenders communicate scoring priorities.
Whether team strategy changes with the scoreboard.

commonErrors.error: Players repeatedly force the three-point score.
commonErrors.correction: Reward decision quality during review, not only total points.

commonErrors.error: Side gates are ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Temporarily double their value to encourage awareness.

commonErrors.error: Players focus on scoring and lose possession structure.
commonErrors.correction: Require one supporting player behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Defenders guard only the end zone.
commonErrors.correction: Assign responsibility for side-gate pressure.

commonErrors.error: Teams do not adjust to the scoreboard.
commonErrors.correction: Announce clear score-and-time scenarios before each round.

progressions: Remove one scoring method during play.
Apply a disposal limit before a scoring attempt.
Add a bonus for consecutive different scoring methods.
Finish with a two-minute live scoreboard scenario.
regressions: Allow the coach to identify the best scoring option during early rounds.
successIndicators: Select scoring options according to pressure and numbers.
Retain possession when the high-value option is unavailable.
Adjust team strategy to the scoreboard.
matchApplication: The game develops the same tactical judgement required when deciding whether to attack directly, retain possession, switch play or accept a lower-risk territorial gain.

title: Freeze, Review and Replay
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise tactical problems, receive concise feedback and immediately apply an improved solution.
setup:
Create a directional small-sided field with scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Nominate one on-field leader for each team.
The coach identifies two or three tactical themes to observe.
Themes may include spacing, support, turnover reaction, scoring choice or defensive shape.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams play a normal directional small-sided game.
The coach allows play to develop before calling “freeze”.
All players stop in their current positions.
The coach asks one or two players what they can see.
The coach provides one concise correction or asks the team to identify a solution.
Players return to the position immediately before the problem developed.
The same passage is replayed with players attempting the improved solution.
If the correction is applied successfully, play continues live.
On-field leaders receive opportunities to conduct selected reviews.
The number of stoppages is limited so the game retains flow.
coachingPoints: Freeze the game only when the tactical picture is clear.
Ask players to describe the problem before giving the answer.
Keep feedback limited to one or two key actions.
Replay the same moment so learning becomes practical.
Encourage players away from the football to explain their role.
Reinforce successful correction immediately.
Allow on-field leaders to provide feedback where appropriate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the tactical issue.
Whether feedback is understood by all relevant players.
Whether the replay produces a visible improvement.
Whether on-field leaders communicate clearly.
Whether the coach avoids excessive interruption.
Whether corrected behaviours transfer into later live play.

commonErrors.error: The coach explains for too long.
commonErrors.correction: Limit feedback to one problem and one solution.

commonErrors.error: Players listen passively.
commonErrors.correction: Ask players to identify space, numbers and options first.

commonErrors.error: The replay begins from a different picture.
commonErrors.correction: Reset players and football to the original positions.

commonErrors.error: Only the ball carrier is questioned.
commonErrors.correction: Include off-ball attackers and defenders in the review.

commonErrors.error: Play is stopped too frequently.
commonErrors.correction: Set a maximum number of freezes per round.

progressions: Allow team leaders to call tactical freezes.
Require players to solve the problem without coach instruction.
Use video recording for post-session comparison.
Remove freezes and assess whether the corrected behaviour remains.
regressions: Use passive defenders during the replay.
Provide two possible solutions for players to choose between.
Reduce the field size and player numbers.
Conduct the first reviews without scoreboard pressure.
successIndicators: Apply feedback during the immediate replay.
Retain the corrected behaviour during later live play.
Take increasing responsibility for team organisation.
matchApplication: The game improves players’ ability to recognise patterns, solve tactical problems and make adjustments during breaks in play, quarter-time discussions and on-field communication.

title: Small-Sided Game Fundamentals Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply the fundamental technical, tactical and behavioural principles introduced across the first small-sided-game block.
setup:
Create a directional field with one scoring zone at each end.
Add one side scoring gate on each side of the field.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
End-zone kick-to-mark scores three points.
End-zone handball receive scores two points.
Side-gate disposal scores one point and retains possession.
The coach prepares assessment categories covering spacing, support, decision making, transition and communication.
Play is conducted in four structured rounds.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one is a three-minute free-play observation round.
Round two introduces a three-second disposal limit.
Round three adds a neutral player supporting the team in possession.
Round four removes the neutral player and uses a live scoreboard scenario.
Possession changes after interceptions, errors, out-of-bounds disposals or infringements.
Players may use any legal disposal and scoring method.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without stopping play unnecessarily.
Between rounds, teams receive one minute to review their own performance.
The coach may provide one priority correction before the next round.
The final score combines game points and assessed team-behaviour points.
coachingPoints: Maintain clear attacking direction.
Create width and depth around the football.
Provide forward, lateral and release options.
Clear scoring space before leading into it.
React immediately when possession changes.
Use numerical advantage before the defence recovers.
Select scoring methods according to risk and opportunity.
Communicate team roles before, during and after possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain purposeful attacking direction.
Whether support triangles form around the ball carrier.
Whether players create and protect scoring space.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.
Whether teams recognise and use numerical advantage.
Whether players balance corridor and wide options.
Whether decisions remain effective under time pressure.
Whether communication improves team organisation.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on the scoreboard.
commonErrors.correction: Award assessment points for spacing, transition and decision quality.

commonErrors.error: Team shape collapses around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Pause between rounds and reset width, depth and support roles.

commonErrors.error: Turnover reaction becomes slow under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce round length and reinforce immediate role changes.

commonErrors.error: Players force high-value scoring options.
commonErrors.correction: Review whether the selected option matched the available pressure.

commonErrors.error: Communication decreases during intense play.
commonErrors.correction: Assign clear on-field leadership responsibilities.

progressions: Remove all scoring explanations and require players to manage independently.
Add score-and-time consequences to each turnover.
Use uneven numbers for selected rounds.
Increase the field size and running demand.
Conduct individual player assessments by position or role.
regressions: Assess only two behavioural categories at a time.
successIndicators: Maintain effective width, depth and directional movement.
Use scoring space with appropriate timing.
Communicate and organise without constant coach instruction.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the fundamental behaviours required in Australian football small-sided games: possession, spacing, forward movement, scoring decisions, turnover reaction, team defence and tactical communication.

title: Boundary Escape Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to retain possession near the boundary and escape pressure through intelligent support, disposal selection and movement back towards open space.
setup:
Create a directional rectangular field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark a four-metre-wide boundary lane along one side of the playing area.
Divide players into two even teams.
The coach begins each passage by delivering the football to a player inside the boundary lane.
The possession team attacks the scoring zone at the opposite end.
Defenders attempt to trap possession against the marked boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts each passage with a disposal to an attacker inside the boundary lane.
Defenders immediately close space and attempt to prevent the football returning to the central area.
The possession team may kick or handball to escape the boundary trap.
At least one support player must provide an option behind or inside the ball carrier.
Once the football leaves the boundary lane, normal directional play continues.
A clean receive inside the attacking scoring zone earns one point.
The defending team earns one point if it forces the football out of bounds or wins possession inside the boundary lane.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Restart from the opposite boundary after each score or stoppage.
Play two- to three-minute rounds before changing the starting side.
coachingPoints: Position the body between the defender and the football.
Look inside before disposing further along the boundary.
Maintain a release option behind the ball carrier.
Use short, accurate disposals to escape immediate pressure.
Do not crowd the boundary lane with multiple support players.
Accelerate into open space once the football is released centrally.
Defenders should use the boundary as an extra defender.
Communicate whether the safest exit is inside, behind or forward.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier protects the football near the boundary.
Whether support players create clear inside and behind options.
Whether attackers avoid sending repeated disposals down the line without advantage.
Whether defenders close central exits while maintaining pressure.
Whether the possession team spreads after escaping the boundary lane.
Whether turnover reactions remain immediate.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier disposes blindly down the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Require an inside scan before each disposal.

commonErrors.error: Support players crowd the same narrow lane.
commonErrors.correction: Position one option inside and one option behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The release player stands still.
commonErrors.correction: Lead laterally to create a clear disposal angle.

commonErrors.error: Defenders attack individually and leave an inside gap.
commonErrors.correction: Coordinate one player pressuring and one protecting the inside exit.

commonErrors.error: Attackers relax after escaping the trap.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate spread and forward support.

progressions: Begin with two defenders pressing the initial receiver.
Introduce full legal tackling for suitable groups.
Award two points for escaping centrally within three disposals.
Require the first disposal from the boundary lane to be a handball.
Begin selected passages with a loose ground ball inside the lane.
regressions: Increase the width of the boundary lane.
Add a neutral release player inside the field.
Delay defensive pressure for two seconds.
Allow the possession team an additional player.
Begin with the football stationary in the attacker’s hands.
successIndicators: Identify central or backward release options.
Maintain useful spacing around the ball carrier.
Escape pressure without conceding an immediate turnover.
Spread quickly once the football returns to open space.
Use the boundary effectively when defending.
matchApplication: The game replicates situations where possession is trapped against the boundary and players must use support, composure and accurate disposal to return the football to safer central space.

title: Four-Corner Target Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to scan the whole playing area and transfer possession towards the least-defended scoring target.
setup:
Mark a square playing area.
Create a three-metre target zone in each corner.
Divide players into two teams.
Each team may score in any corner.
A player cannot remain inside a corner target zone while waiting for possession.
The receiver must enter the zone after the disposal is released.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play in the centre of the square.
The team in possession attempts to complete a disposal to a teammate entering any corner target zone.
A successful receive earns one point.
After scoring, the same team retains possession but cannot use the same corner again immediately.
Defenders attempt to protect the nearest targets while applying pressure to the football.
A turnover changes possession but does not change the available scoring targets.
Players must continually scan for an open corner as the defensive shape moves.
The football may be kicked or handballed.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
Teams rotate starting possession between rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan all four corners before receiving.
Move the defence towards one side before switching to another target.
Maintain support behind the football during a switch.
Enter the target zone with timing rather than waiting inside it.
Use shorter disposals to reposition defenders before attempting to score.
Communicate when a corner becomes available.
Defenders should protect multiple targets through central positioning.
Avoid forcing possession into a corner that is already crowded.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan away from the immediate contest.
Whether the possession team changes direction when a target is defended.
Whether receivers time their entry into target zones.
Whether players support the football during switches.
Whether defenders maintain positions that protect more than one corner.
Whether teams use patience without becoming static.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on the nearest corner.
commonErrors.correction: Require the ball carrier to identify a second target before disposing.

commonErrors.error: Receivers wait inside target zones.
commonErrors.correction: Disallow the score unless the player enters after the disposal.

commonErrors.error: The football is switched too slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage early movement and quicker lateral disposal.

commonErrors.error: Support disappears behind a long switch.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one player behind the football as turnover protection.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase individual opponents into corners.
commonErrors.correction: Coach central positioning that protects multiple targets.

progressions: Award two points for scoring in the corner furthest from the previous score.
Require one kick during every scoring chain.
Nominate one temporarily inactive corner during play.
regressions: Permit consecutive scores in the same corner.
Stop briefly after turnovers to allow teams to reorganise.
successIndicators: Move the defence before changing direction.
Maintain support and possession during switches.
Defend several potential targets through intelligent positioning.
matchApplication: The game develops the ability to change the point of attack, shift defensive structures and use open space rather than forcing possession into congestion.

title: Dispose and Replace
objective: Develop players’ habit of moving immediately after disposal and replacing vacated positions to maintain team shape and continuous support.
setup:
Create a directional rectangular field with a scoring zone at each end.
Place four positional markers through the middle of the playing area.
Divide players into two teams.
Players may move freely, but the team in possession must maintain at least one player in each marked positional area.
Teams score through a clean receive inside the attacking scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
After disposing, the player must immediately leave their current positional area.
A teammate replaces the vacated area to maintain team shape.
The disposal recipient must scan before receiving and identify the next movement.
Players may kick or handball.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A bonus point is awarded when the scoring chain includes three successful position replacements.
Possession changes after an interception, error or infringement.
The replacement rule immediately applies to the new possession team.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Move as soon as the disposal leaves the hands or foot.
Replace space rather than following the football.
Maintain width and depth across the playing area.
Communicate who is filling each vacated position.
Time replacement movement so the next ball carrier has multiple options.
Avoid rotating every player in the same direction.
Defenders should track movement while protecting dangerous space.
Continue moving after scoring or losing possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Whether vacated positions are replaced.
Whether team shape remains balanced.
Whether movement creates useful options rather than unnecessary rotation.
Whether defenders communicate when opponents exchange positions.
Whether replacement behaviour continues under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Make movement after disposal a scoring requirement.

commonErrors.error: Everyone follows the football.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the nearest teammate to replace the vacated space instead.

commonErrors.error: Players rotate into already occupied areas.
commonErrors.correction: Require communication before replacing.

commonErrors.error: Team width disappears.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one outside position occupied on each side.

commonErrors.error: Defenders follow opponents and abandon dangerous space.
commonErrors.correction: Defend the space first and transfer opponents through communication.

progressions: Require the disposer to create an overlap before re-entering possession.
Remove positional markers once the movement pattern is established.
Award defensive points for preventing effective replacement.
regressions: Allow the coach to nominate the replacement player.
Pause briefly after each disposal during the introductory round.
successIndicators: Preserve team shape during possession changes.
matchApplication: The game reinforces the movement required after disposal to create overlap, maintain attacking structure and prevent players from becoming stationary behind the football.

title: Mark or Play-On Choice
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when to play on immediately after a mark and when to hold possession and assess safer options.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
Normal marking rules apply.
A player who marks may play on immediately or hold possession for up to five seconds.
Teams score through a marked kick inside the attacking scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play near the centre.
Teams move the football towards their attacking scoring zone.
After taking a mark, the player must decide whether to play on or hold possession.
A successful play-on disposal completed within two seconds earns a tempo bonus marker.
A player who holds possession may use up to five seconds to scan and select an option.
Three tempo bonus markers convert to one additional point.
A marked kick inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A handball receive inside the zone earns one point.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
The coach reviews selected decisions between rounds rather than stopping every passage.
coachingPoints: Scan before the football arrives.
Play on when space, numbers and a clear next option are available.
Hold possession when the forward path is blocked or support has not formed.
Do not play on simply to earn a bonus.
Move quickly when a teammate marks and may play on.
Defenders must recover immediately rather than assuming the mark will stop play.
Use the protected possession period to organise width and depth.
Communicate “go”, “hold” or directional information early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the marking player scans before gaining possession.
Whether play-on decisions produce genuine advantage.
Whether players hold possession appropriately when forward options are poor.
Whether teammates react quickly to marks.
Whether defenders continue recovering after a mark.
Whether communication supports the decision.

commonErrors.error: Players automatically play on after every mark.
commonErrors.correction: Reward only play-on decisions that create advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players always stop and slow the game.
commonErrors.correction: Highlight open space and encourage earlier scanning.

commonErrors.error: Support players stop when a mark is taken.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate movement until the umpire or coach calls time.

commonErrors.error: Defenders relax after conceding a mark.
commonErrors.correction: Continue defensive recovery and protect the next option.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier uses the full five seconds without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require active head movement and early option identification.

progressions: Reduce the hold period to three seconds.
Add full legal pressure after play-on.
Award defensive points for forcing poor play-on decisions.
Introduce scoreboard scenarios requiring fast or controlled play.
Require the player taking a mark to verbally call “go” or “hold”.
regressions: Allow the coach to cue play-on decisions during early rounds.
successIndicators: Play on when clear advantage exists.
Hold possession when structure must reset.
Support both fast and controlled ball movement.
matchApplication: The game replicates the frequent match decision following a mark: attack quickly before the defence resets or control possession until a safer option develops.

title: Ground-Ball Launch Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to win a contested or pressured ground ball and immediately launch an organised attacking possession.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Place three ground-ball starting markers across the centre.
Divide players into two even teams.
Each passage starts with the coach rolling, bouncing or releasing a loose football towards one marker.
Players begin at least five metres from the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases a ground ball into the central area.
One or more players from each team compete to win possession.
The player collecting the football must protect it and dispose legally.
Teammates provide immediate inside, outside and rear support.
The team that wins possession attacks its nominated scoring end.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within four disposals of the ground-ball win earns two points.
If the opposition wins the football during the passage, it attacks the opposite end.
After a score or stoppage, players reset for a new ground-ball release.
Rotate starting positions regularly.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with a low, balanced body position.
Keep the body between the opponent and the football.
Take the football cleanly when possible rather than tapping without purpose.
Provide immediate support on more than one side.
Use the first disposal to escape congestion.
Accelerate after the release disposal.
Communicate whether the player has time, pressure or support.
Defenders should pressure the release without all collapsing into the contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
The approach and body position at the ground ball.
Whether players attempt clean possession when appropriate.
Whether support arrives before the ball is won.
Whether the first disposal exits pressure.
Whether teammates spread after the ground-ball win.
Whether defenders maintain structure outside the contest.
Whether contact remains controlled and legal.

commonErrors.error: Players overrun the football.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and lower the body early.

commonErrors.error: The winner stands upright in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Stay low, protect the football and release quickly.

commonErrors.error: Teammates wait to see who wins possession.
commonErrors.correction: Move into support positions before possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: All players collapse into the ground-ball contest.
commonErrors.correction: Keep outside players available for release or defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal goes back into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the open side before collecting.

progressions: Start with a two-versus-two ground-ball contest.
Introduce full legal tackling for suitable players.
Award bonus points for a clean one-touch collection.
Add a second ground ball after the first score.
regressions: Begin with an uncontested ground-ball collection.
successIndicators: Protect possession with sound body position.
Spread and attack immediately after winning the football.
Retain defensive structure outside the contest.
matchApplication: The game replicates loose-ball situations where the team that wins possession must quickly escape congestion and convert the contest win into attacking movement.

title: Split-Zone Reconnection Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to reconnect defensive, midfield and attacking units through purposeful link movement and well-timed disposals.
setup:
Divide a rectangular field into defensive, midfield and attacking thirds.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin with at least one player from each team in every third.
Players may move between thirds, but a team must retain at least one player in each zone.
The football must travel through the midfield third before entering the attacking third.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in one team’s defensive third.
The possession team attempts to connect through midfield and enter its attacking third.
Players may lead across zone lines to create links.
At least one teammate must replace any player leaving a zone.
A clean receive inside the attacking scoring zone earns one point.
A score created through a one-touch midfield link earns two points.
A turnover immediately changes attacking direction.
The new possession team must reorganise its three-zone structure.
Defenders may press into adjacent zones while preserving team balance.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Create a visible link option between each line.
Lead diagonally rather than directly towards the football.
Time movement across zone lines with the ball carrier’s readiness.
Replace players who leave their zone.
Avoid sending every player ahead of the football.
Use the midfield link to change direction when the direct path is blocked.
Defenders should deny central connections while protecting depth.
Communicate which player is linking and which player is replacing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether each team maintains representation in all three zones.
Whether link players lead at the correct time.
Whether disposals allow receivers to continue moving.
Whether players replace teammates crossing zone lines.
Whether defenders block central links without losing depth.
Whether the team can reconnect after a turnover.

commonErrors.error: The midfield zone becomes empty.
commonErrors.correction: Require a replacement before the link player leaves.

commonErrors.error: Players lead directly towards the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Use diagonal movement to create a clearer lane.

commonErrors.error: Disposals arrive after the lead has closed.
commonErrors.correction: Encourage earlier scanning and release.

commonErrors.error: Too many players move into the attacking third.
commonErrors.correction: Retain support behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the ball and lose deep coverage.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one player protecting the next zone.

progressions: Reduce the width of the midfield third.
Require a one-touch disposal from the first midfield receiver.
Allow defenders to create temporary numerical pressure in one zone.
Remove zone restrictions during the final round.
Award defensive points for intercepting a line-breaking disposal.
regressions: Begin each possession with protected use in the defensive third.
successIndicators: Maintain team connection across all three zones.
Create and use effective link players.
Time leads with the ball carrier’s disposal.
matchApplication: The game develops connection between defensive, midfield and forward lines, reducing isolated units and improving controlled movement through the ground.

title: Protect the Hot Spot
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to protect the most dangerous central scoring space while still applying pressure to the ball carrier and wider options.
setup:
Create a directional field.
Mark a central five-metre hot-spot scoring zone at each end.
Mark one wider scoring zone on either side of each hot spot.
Divide players into two teams.
A marked kick received inside the hot spot earns three points.
A receive in either wider zone earns one point.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams attack their nominated scoring end.
The possession team attempts to create and use any scoring zone.
A clean mark inside the central hot spot earns three points.
A legal receive inside a wider zone earns one point.
Defenders must protect the hot spot while pressuring the football and wider leads.
A defensive intercept inside the hot spot earns one defensive point.
Following a turnover, the intercepting team immediately attacks the opposite end.
Players may kick or handball outside the scoring zones.
The coach records both attacking and defensive points.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Defenders should position themselves goal side and corridor side.
The nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
Deeper defenders protect the hot spot and communicate passing responsibility.
Do not abandon central space to chase a low-value wide option.
Attackers should use width to move defenders before attacking the hot spot.
Entry disposals must favour the receiver.
Intercepting defenders should transition quickly before the opposition resets.
Defensive communication must begin before the entry disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders protect central scoring space.
Whether the nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
Whether deeper defenders communicate and pass opponents.
Whether attackers move defenders before entering centrally.
Whether wide scoring options are used appropriately.
Whether defensive intercepts lead to immediate transition.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all press the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one pressure player and retain central protection.

commonErrors.error: A defender follows an opponent wide and opens the hot spot.
commonErrors.correction: Pass the wide opponent to a teammate and remain goal side.

commonErrors.error: Attackers repeatedly kick to a crowded hot spot.
commonErrors.correction: Use wide possession to shift the defensive structure first.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch the football and lose opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Check both the ball carrier and dangerous space.

commonErrors.error: Interceptors stop after winning possession.
commonErrors.correction: Require an immediate release disposal or run.

progressions: Increase the hot-spot value to five points.
Allow attackers only eight seconds to enter a scoring zone.
Award defensive points for forcing a wide score.
Begin selected passages with the defence temporarily outnumbered.
regressions: Reduce scoring to one central and one wide zone.
Begin with passive pressure on the ball carrier.
Allow defenders to remain stationed inside the hot spot.
successIndicators: Apply pressure without losing defensive shape.
matchApplication: The game replicates team defence inside defensive 50, where players must protect the most dangerous central area without conceding uncontested possession elsewhere.

title: Live Target Call Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to process a changing external cue and rapidly reorganise attacking and defensive behaviour towards a newly active target.
setup:
Create a square playing area.
Place one numbered scoring gate on each side.
Divide players into two teams.
All gates remain physically available, but only the gate called by the coach is active.
The coach holds number cards or uses clear verbal calls.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins as a possession game in the centre.
The coach calls or displays the number of the active scoring gate.
The team in possession immediately attempts to complete a disposal through that gate.
The defending team reorganises to protect the active gate.
The coach may change the active gate while the football is moving.
A completed disposal through the active gate earns one point.
A disposal through an inactive gate does not score and results in a turnover.
Following a score, the opposition begins with possession.
The coach varies the timing of target changes.
Play continues in ninety-second high-intensity rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan the coach’s cue and the field simultaneously.
Communicate the active target immediately.
Reorient body position before receiving.
Use the nearest safe option to change the point of attack.
Do not force a direct disposal if the target is heavily defended.
Defenders should protect the active gate while maintaining pressure.
Players away from the football must move first when the target changes.
Continue reacting until the score or turnover is confirmed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players identify the active target.
Whether off-ball players react before the ball carrier.
Whether body position changes with the new direction.
Whether teams use support to redirect possession.
Whether defenders communicate and reorganise.
Whether players remain composed after sudden target changes.

commonErrors.error: Players continue towards the previous target.
commonErrors.correction: Require teammates to repeat the new call aloud.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier turns without support.
commonErrors.correction: Off-ball players must move immediately when the cue changes.

commonErrors.error: Teams force a direct pass through congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use one or two support disposals to reposition the defence.

commonErrors.error: Defenders protect the new gate but stop pressuring the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain both gate protection and ball pressure.

commonErrors.error: Players watch the coach and lose awareness of opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Scan briefly, communicate and return visual attention to play.

progressions: Activate two gates with different point values.
Allow a player leader to make selected target calls.
regressions: Keep each target active for a full possession.
Announce the next target before it becomes active.
successIndicators: Reorient body position and team shape.
matchApplication: The game develops rapid response to changing match information, including turnovers, umpire calls, team instructions, open space and shifting scoring opportunities.

title: Reset or Attack Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when to attack forward immediately and when to reset possession to create a better opportunity.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark one reset zone five metres behind the central line on each side.
Divide players into two teams.
Teams may attack the scoring zone directly or use their reset zone to retain possession and reorganise.
A player receiving in the reset zone is protected from pressure for two seconds.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play starts near the centre.
The possession team assesses whether a forward opportunity is available.
If advantage exists, the team may attack the scoring zone immediately.
If the forward path is blocked, the football may be transferred into the reset zone.
A reset-zone receiver has two seconds of protected possession.
The team must spread and create a new attacking shape during the reset.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score achieved without using the reset zone earns a bonus point when the decision was successful.
If a forced direct attack results in a turnover, the opposition receives a transition bonus point if it scores from the next possession.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan forward immediately after gaining possession.
Attack when space, numbers and support are available.
Reset when the defence has superior numbers or central space is blocked.
Do not reset automatically when a clear forward option exists.
Use the protected reset period to create width and depth.
Maintain players ahead of the football during a reset.
Defenders should press the reset receiver after protection expires.
Communicate whether the team is attacking quickly or controlling possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan forward before resetting.
Whether direct attacks are based on genuine advantage.
Whether resets improve team shape.
Whether players ahead of the football remain active.
Whether defenders reorganise during the protected period.
Whether communication establishes the intended tempo.

commonErrors.error: Teams reset every possession.
commonErrors.correction: Reward early forward use when clear advantage exists.

commonErrors.error: Players force forward disposals into superior numbers.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the reset option before receiving.

commonErrors.error: The team remains narrow during the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Use the protected period to establish width and depth.

commonErrors.error: All players move behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain at least two forward options.

commonErrors.error: The reset receiver holds the football without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate head movement and communication.

progressions: Reduce protected reset time to one second.
Limit teams to one reset per possession.
Apply scoreboard scenarios requiring fast or controlled play.
Award defensive points for forcing repeated resets.
regressions: Increase reset protection to four seconds.
Coach the attack-or-reset decision during the first round.
successIndicators: Reset possession when the forward path is blocked.
Control tempo according to the tactical situation.
matchApplication: The game replicates decisions made during defensive exits, transition and possession chains where teams must choose between immediate attack and controlled ball retention.

title: Player-Led Fundamentals Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to independently organise, play and adjust a small-sided game using the fundamental principles established across SG-001 to SG-019.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Add optional side scoring gates.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Each team selects an on-field leader.
Provide teams with three minutes to decide their preferred attacking shape, defensive priority and turnover response.
The coach establishes only the safety rules, scoring system and playing time.
Players manage positioning, communication and tactical adjustments.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin with a player-led planning period.
Each team identifies its attacking structure, defensive structure and turnover roles.
Play begins as a directional small-sided game.
A kick-to-mark inside the scoring zone earns three points.
A handball receive inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A completed disposal through a side gate earns one point and retains possession.
The coach observes without directing routine decisions.
At the end of each four-minute round, teams receive ninety seconds to review and adjust.
On-field leaders organise changes before the next round.
The final round is played without a formal break or coach instruction.
After play, each team explains one successful adjustment and one area requiring improvement.
coachingPoints: Establish clear width, depth and support roles.
Communicate attacking direction and scoring priorities.
Protect dangerous central space when defending.
React immediately when possession changes.
Use numerical advantage and open space.
Decide when to attack quickly and when to reset.
Allow on-field leaders to coordinate without dominating every decision.
Make tactical adjustments based on observable evidence.
Maintain legal, controlled contact and safe play.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether teams establish a clear structure without detailed coach direction.
Whether players maintain spacing and support.
Whether communication is shared across the team.
Whether leaders organise rather than simply demand the football.
Whether teams react effectively to turnovers.
Whether tactical adjustments address actual problems.
Whether players choose appropriate scoring methods.
Whether corrected behaviours remain during the final uninterrupted round.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for the coach to solve problems.
commonErrors.correction: Direct questions back to the team during review periods.

commonErrors.error: One leader controls every decision.
commonErrors.correction: Require contributions from several players.

commonErrors.error: Team structure disappears once play becomes intense.
commonErrors.correction: Ask players to identify their reference positions before restarting.

commonErrors.error: Reviews focus only on mistakes with the football.
commonErrors.correction: Include spacing, defence, transition and communication.

commonErrors.error: Teams make changes unrelated to the observed problem.
commonErrors.correction: Require each adjustment to include a clear reason.

progressions: Allow teams to design their own scoring system.
Give each team a different hidden tactical objective.
Record the game for player-led video review.
regressions: Provide teams with a simple planning template.
Limit the game to one scoring method.
Allow the coach to ask guiding questions during reviews.
Reduce team numbers and field size.
Predetermine one attacking and one defensive principle.
successIndicators: Select appropriate attacking tempo and scoring methods.
matchApplication: The game prepares players to organise and adapt during matches when coaches cannot direct every action, requiring leadership, communication, tactical awareness and collective problem solving.

title: Overlap Lane Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to create and use overlap run through coordinated movement after disposal.
setup:
Divide the field lengthways into three lanes.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
Players may move between lanes.
A player who disposes must attempt to run into an adjacent lane and provide an overlap option.
Teams score by completing a disposal to a teammate inside the attacking scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play near the centre.
The team in possession attacks its nominated scoring end.
After disposing, the player must accelerate into an adjacent lane.
The receiver may return the football to the overlapping player or use another option.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score involving a successful overlap possession earns two points.
Defenders may track the overlapping runner or transfer responsibility.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Teams play three-minute rounds.
Change attacking directions between rounds.
coachingPoints: Accelerate immediately after disposal.
Run beyond the receiver rather than stopping beside them.
Use width so the overlap runner does not enter the same pressure line.
Draw a defender before releasing the football.
Time the return handball so the runner receives at speed.
Do not force the return disposal if a better option is available.
Defenders should communicate whether to track or transfer the runner.
Maintain support behind the football in case the overlap is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the disposer accelerates immediately.
Whether overlap run enters useful space.
Whether the receiver draws pressure before releasing.
Whether players force the return disposal unnecessarily.
Whether defenders communicate responsibility.
Whether the possession team retains balance behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The disposer jogs after releasing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require a five-metre acceleration before slowing.

commonErrors.error: The overlap runner enters the same lane as the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Use an adjacent lane to widen the defensive problem.

commonErrors.error: The return handball is released too early.
commonErrors.correction: Draw the defender before giving the football back.

commonErrors.error: Players force every overlap.
commonErrors.correction: Use the runner only when the option creates advantage.

commonErrors.error: Defenders both follow the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate who tracks the runner and who pressures the football.

progressions: Reduce the width of each lane.
Award a bonus for two consecutive overlaps.
Add full legal tackling for suitable players.
Require the overlap runner to receive in the forward half.
Remove lane markers after movement habits improve.
regressions: Allow the overlap runner protected possession.
Require only one overlap attempt per possession.
successIndicators: Run beyond the next ball carrier.
Release the football after drawing pressure.
Use overlap only when it creates advantage.
matchApplication: The game develops running support used during defensive exits, midfield transition and attacking chains when a player releases the football and continues forward to create an extra number.

title: Give-and-Go Gate Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to complete a short disposal, accelerate into space and receive the football again beyond defensive pressure.
setup:
Create a directional playing area.
Place four two-metre movement gates through the middle.
Divide players into two teams.
A player may score a movement bonus by disposing, running through a gate and receiving again.
Teams score normally through a receive inside the attacking scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
Players move the football towards their attacking end.
After disposing, a player may accelerate through a nearby movement gate.
If the player receives the football again after passing through the gate, the team earns one movement bonus.
A scoring-zone receive earns one match point.
Two movement bonuses during the same possession add one extra match point.
Defenders attempt to block the return lane or pressure the receiver.
A turnover immediately changes attacking direction.
Movement bonuses reset after every turnover.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Dispose accurately before accelerating.
Run through the gate at speed rather than drifting.
Create a clear return angle.
The receiver should protect the football and assess whether the return option is safe.
Use short, controlled handballs or kicks suited to the available space.
Avoid several players using the same gate.
Defenders should recover goal side and block the return lane.
Continue supporting if the give-and-go is denied.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players accelerate after disposal.
Whether the return angle remains clear.
Whether the ball carrier selects a suitable return option.
Whether several attackers crowd one movement gate.
Whether defenders recover between the runner and the scoring end.
Whether the movement continues when the return disposal is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Players run slowly through gates.
commonErrors.correction: Require a genuine acceleration to earn the bonus.

commonErrors.error: The return receiver runs directly behind a defender.
commonErrors.correction: Change the running angle before calling for the football.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces the return disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Use another option when the defender closes the lane.

commonErrors.error: Several attackers use the same gate.
commonErrors.correction: Scan for an unoccupied gate before moving.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch the football and lose the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Check the disposer’s movement immediately after pressure is applied.

progressions: Require the return possession to be completed within three seconds.
Award two bonuses when the return player disposes forward immediately.
Remove one gate during each round.
regressions: Allow protected possession after passing through a gate.
Count the movement bonus without requiring a return possession.
successIndicators: Continue moving when the initial give-and-go is denied.
matchApplication: The game develops short give-and-go combinations used to escape congestion, break defensive lines and continue running support through the middle of the ground.

title: Third-Player Run Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to create attacking advantage through the movement of a third player who is not directly involved in the initial disposal.
setup:
Create a directional field with scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Within each team, nominate temporary groups of three.
The third player in a chain is the teammate who was not the passer or immediate receiver.
Teams earn bonus points when that third player becomes the next effective receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play with one team.
Player A disposes to Player B.
Player C, who was not involved in the first disposal, moves into a new supporting or attacking position.
If Player B disposes successfully to Player C, the team earns one movement bonus.
The chain may continue with a new third player.
A scoring-zone receive earns one match point.
A score immediately following a third-player movement bonus earns two match points.
Defenders attempt to identify and track the third-player runner.
A turnover changes attacking direction and resets the movement bonus.
Rotate nominated groups between rounds.
coachingPoints: The third player should move as the first disposal travels.
Run into space that neither the passer nor receiver occupies.
Create a forward, lateral or overlap option according to pressure.
The immediate receiver should scan beyond the nearest support.
Do not delay the second disposal until the third-player advantage disappears.
Communicate the third-player movement early.
Defenders must scan away from the football and transfer responsibility.
Keep another support option behind the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the third player moves before the first disposal is completed.
Whether the movement creates a genuinely new option.
Whether the immediate receiver scans early.
Whether the second disposal is released before defensive recovery.
Whether defenders track players away from the football.
Whether the possession team retains balance behind the chain.

commonErrors.error: The third player waits until the receiver has possession.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement while the first disposal is travelling.

commonErrors.error: The third player runs into the same space as the passer.
commonErrors.correction: Move into a different lane or depth.

commonErrors.error: The receiver looks only back to the original passer.
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward and laterally before receiving.

commonErrors.error: The second disposal is delayed.
commonErrors.correction: Release the football while the runner still has separation.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all focus on the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Assign communication responsibility for off-ball runners.

progressions: Require the third-player receive to occur within four seconds.
Award bonus points for a third-player run into the scoring zone.
Remove nominated groups and allow players to identify the pattern naturally.
Add a second active football for advanced observation work.
regressions: Nominate the third-player runner before each possession.
Allow protected possession for the immediate receiver.
Use handball only during introductory rounds.
successIndicators: Create options away from the immediate disposal pair.
Release the second disposal before pressure closes.
matchApplication: The game develops off-ball running patterns that create overlap, line breaks and uncontested possession beyond the immediate ball carrier and receiver.

title: Moving Mark Target Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to create, identify and complete moving marking options during continuous small-sided play.
setup:
Create a directional playing area with a scoring zone at each end.
Place two lead-start markers in each half.
Divide players into two teams.
A mark only counts when the receiver is moving at the moment of contact.
Teams score through a moving mark inside the attacking scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins near the centre.
Teams move the football towards their attacking end.
Players create leads from the start markers or from open space.
A mark taken while moving earns one possession bonus.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A stationary uncontested mark retains possession but does not earn a bonus.
The marking player may hold possession or play on.
Defenders may track, block legal space and attempt to spoil.
A turnover changes attacking direction.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Begin leads from space rather than from beside the ball carrier.
Change pace to separate from the defender.
