Lead into the ball carrier’s vision.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage side.
Avoid high, slow disposals that allow defensive recovery.
Mark with hands extended and maintain forward momentum.
Decide whether to play on before completing the mark.
Defenders should remain goal side and close the leading lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether leads begin from usable space.
Whether players change pace.
Whether ball carriers identify the lead early.
Whether kicks favour the receiver’s movement.
Whether marking players remain balanced.
Whether defenders track the lead without losing dangerous space.
Whether play-on decisions create advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players stand and call for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require movement before the disposal can be directed to them.

commonErrors.error: Leads run directly at the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Lead diagonally to create a clearer kicking lane.

commonErrors.error: Kicks land behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Aim into the receiver’s path.

commonErrors.error: Players slow before marking.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain movement and extend the hands.

commonErrors.error: Defenders trail directly behind.
commonErrors.correction: Start goal side and influence the lead away from danger.

progressions: Require every second possession to be a kick.
Add full legal bodywork for suitable players.
Award three points for a mark followed by an immediate effective play-on.
Require double leads before scoring-zone entry.
regressions: Remove scoring pressure during the first round.
matchApplication: The game replicates marking options created through movement during transition, forward entry and controlled possession.

title: Inside-Outside Release Game
objective: Develop coordinated inside and outside movement so contested possession can be released into open space.
setup:
Mark a central contest zone approximately eight metres wide.
Mark one outside lane on each side.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Each possession begins with a loose football inside the central zone.
At least one player from each team must begin in each outside lane.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases a loose football into the central contest zone.
Players compete to win possession.
The team that wins the football attempts to release it to a teammate in an outside lane.
Once the football reaches an outside player, all players may move freely.
The team attacks its nominated scoring zone.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score created from a clean inside-to-outside release earns two points.
If the opposition intercepts the release, it immediately attacks the opposite end.
Players reset after each score or stoppage.
Rotate starting inside and outside roles.
coachingPoints: Inside players should remain strong and balanced over the football.
Outside players must hold width until possession is clearly won.
Communicate the open release side early.
Use handball to move the football away from congestion.
The release player should receive while moving forward.
Do not send every player into the initial contest.
Defenders should pressure the release while protecting the scoring side.
Spread immediately after the football exits congestion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether outside players maintain width.
Whether inside players protect and release the football.
Whether communication identifies the open side.
Whether the outside receiver is moving.
Whether too many players enter the contest.
Whether the possession team transitions rapidly after release.
Whether defenders pressure without abandoning structure.

commonErrors.error: Outside players enter the contest too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the outside lane until the football is clearly won.

commonErrors.error: The inside player attempts a difficult kick from congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use a short handball to release pressure first.

commonErrors.error: The outside receiver stands still.
commonErrors.correction: Move forward or laterally as possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: All defenders collapse inside.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one defender positioned to pressure the release.

commonErrors.error: The release handball goes behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Direct it into the receiver’s forward path.

progressions: Reduce the width of the outside lanes.
Begin with a two-versus-two or three-versus-three ground-ball contest.
Require the first outside possession to be used within two seconds.
Award defensive points for intercepting the release.
Remove lane restrictions after the initial contest.
regressions: Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
Allow the release receiver protected possession.
successIndicators: Deliver the football into the receiver’s path.
matchApplication: The game develops the inside-outside structure used at stoppages, ground-ball contests and congested phases to release possession into space.

title: Switch-and-Surge Game
primarySkill: Accelerating after a switch of play
objective: Develop players’ ability to switch possession away from pressure and immediately surge forward before the defence can reorganise.
setup:
Divide the field into left, central and right lanes.
Mark scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
A switch is completed when the football moves from one outside lane to the other.
Following a switch, the possession team has eight seconds to attempt a scoring-zone entry.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with the football in one outside lane.
The possession team may attack directly or switch across the field.
When the football reaches the opposite outside lane, the coach begins an eight-second count.
The possession team must surge forward and attempt to score.
A scoring-zone receive following a completed switch earns two points.
A normal scoring-zone receive earns one point.
Defenders attempt to slow the switch, close the far side and recover towards the scoring zone.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
The new possession team may immediately begin its own switch.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Create width before attempting the switch.
Move the football faster than defenders can shift.
The far-side players should move before the switch arrives.
Attack forward immediately after reaching the open side.
Use overlap and third-player run during the surge.
Maintain one support option behind the football.
Defenders should communicate the switch and recover through the corridor.
Do not switch when the far side is already outnumbered.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the possession team creates enough width.
Whether the switch moves quickly.
Whether far-side players move before receiving.
Whether forward run begins immediately after the switch.
Whether one support player remains behind the football.
Whether defenders recover centrally rather than chasing the ball laterally.
Whether teams avoid switching into disadvantage.

commonErrors.error: The switch is slow and allows defensive recovery.
commonErrors.correction: Use fewer, longer or faster disposals across the field.

commonErrors.error: Far-side players wait until the football arrives.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement when the switch starts.

commonErrors.error: The possession team continues moving sideways after the switch.
commonErrors.correction: Attack forward immediately on the open side.

commonErrors.error: No support remains behind the surge.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one player to protect against turnover.

commonErrors.error: Defenders recover directly towards the ball.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through central dangerous space first.

progressions: Reduce the surge time to six seconds.
Require one kick during the switch.
Award a bonus for a moving mark after the switch.
Allow defenders to start with an extra player on the ball side.
regressions: Allow protected possession on the far side.
Begin with the switch already completed.
successIndicators: Move the football quickly across the field.
matchApplication: The game replicates switching possession across half-back or midfield and attacking rapidly through the open side before the opposition can restore defensive shape.

title: Carry-and-Release Advantage
primarySkill: Running with the football to draw pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to carry the football towards pressure, draw a defender and release to a teammate in advantage.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark two carry zones through the middle.
Divide players into two teams.
A player entering a carry zone with possession is encouraged to run and engage a defender before disposing.
Normal running and bouncing rules apply.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
When a ball carrier enters a carry zone, they may accelerate forward.
The ball carrier attempts to draw a defender.
A teammate provides a support option beyond or beside the pressured defender.
A successful release after engaging a defender earns one movement bonus.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following a carry-and-release bonus earns two points.
Defenders attempt to close under control and prevent the release.
A turnover changes attacking direction.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Carry the football into available space.
Keep the head up while running.
Engage the defender without running directly into contact.
Release before being fully closed down.
Support runners should maintain separation from the ball carrier.
Use handball or short kick according to pressure and distance.
Defenders should approach under control and protect the release option.
Retain support behind the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players carry the football when space is available.
Whether the ball carrier keeps scanning.
Whether the defender is genuinely engaged before release.
Whether support runners maintain useful width.
Whether the release disposal leads the receiver.
Whether defenders close without overcommitting.
Whether the team retains shape behind the run.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier disposes before drawing pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry until the defender must commit.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier runs directly into the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Approach on an angle and preserve an escape side.

commonErrors.error: The support runner gets too close.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough separation to prevent one defender covering both players.

commonErrors.error: The release disposal goes behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Handball or kick into the receiver’s path.

commonErrors.error: Defenders charge and lose balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and protect the release lane.

progressions: Award a bonus for breaking a second defensive line.
Apply a three-second limit after entering the carry zone.
Start selected passages with a numerical disadvantage.
regressions: Allow protected possession inside the carry zone.
successIndicators: Defend the carrier and release option with balance.
matchApplication: The game develops the running carry used to engage defenders, create overlap and release teammates into space during transition and attacking ball movement.

title: Rotating Numbers Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust movement, spacing and tactical roles as numerical advantage changes during play.
setup:
Create a directional field with scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Position one or two interchange players from each team beside entry gates.
The coach controls when players enter or leave.
Play may change between equal numbers, attacking advantage and defensive advantage.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play starts with equal numbers.
During play, the coach signals a player to enter or leave.
Teams must recognise the new numerical situation.
A team with extra numbers should spread, move the football and find the spare.
A team outnumbered should delay, protect dangerous space and force play wide.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score while using a temporary numerical advantage earns two points.
A defensive stop while outnumbered earns one defensive point.
Player changes may occur after turnovers or during continuous possession.
Rotate all players through the entry roles.
coachingPoints: Count numbers around the football and ahead of play.
Spread immediately when an extra player enters.
Use the spare before the opposition reorganises.
When outnumbered, slow the attack and protect central space.
Communicate role changes early.
Do not send every extra player towards the football.
Re-establish normal structure when numbers become equal.
Continue scanning for player-entry signals.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly teams recognise number changes.
Whether the team with advantage creates width.
Whether the spare player becomes involved.
Whether the outnumbered team delays and protects dangerous space.
Whether players communicate changing roles.
Whether normal structure returns when numbers equalise.
Whether players continue concentrating away from the football.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to notice the number change.
commonErrors.correction: Require leaders to call the numbers immediately.

commonErrors.error: The extra player joins existing congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Move the spare into a separate lane or depth.

commonErrors.error: The outnumbered team attacks the football recklessly.
commonErrors.correction: Delay and protect central scoring space.

commonErrors.error: Roles remain unchanged when a player leaves.
commonErrors.correction: Reassign pressure, support and protection responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Teams keep playing as if the advantage remains.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate when numbers return to even.

progressions: Allow two players to enter simultaneously.
Begin a round with one team unaware of the exact numbers.
regressions: Stop play briefly when numbers change.
Add a neutral player rather than rotating team numbers.
Announce number changes before they occur.
successIndicators: Restore normal structure when numbers equalise.
matchApplication: The game replicates changing numbers caused by turnovers, rotations, players leaving contests, defensive presses and delayed recovery during match play.

title: Continuous Wave Transition Game
primarySkill: Continuous movement between attack and defence
objective: Develop players’ ability to maintain purposeful movement as they repeatedly transition between attacking and defensive roles.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into three teams.
Two teams play while the third waits behind one scoring end.
The team that scores exits.
The waiting team immediately enters with a new football and attacks the opposite direction.
The team that conceded must transition instantly into defence.
howTheDrillWorks:
Two teams begin live play.
A team scores through a clean receive inside the attacking scoring zone.
The scoring team immediately exits through the end line.
The waiting team enters from that end with a new football.
The team that conceded turns and defends the new attack.
If a turnover occurs before a score, normal play continues.
The entering team should attack before the defending team fully reorganises.
Each team records attacking scores and defensive stops.
Rounds continue for three to four minutes.
Provide recovery between rounds and rotate entry sides.
coachingPoints: React immediately after the score.
The conceding team must turn, communicate and protect central space.
The entering team should spread before receiving the new football.
Attack with speed but retain clean disposal.
Maintain forward and rear support during each wave.
Players exiting must clear the field quickly.
Manage effort so decision quality remains sound.
For Over 35 players, shorten rounds and reduce total repetitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Speed of transition after scores.
Whether defenders protect the corridor first.
Whether the entering team creates width.
Whether players maintain skill execution under fatigue.
Whether exiting players avoid interfering.
Whether communication changes immediately.
Whether workloads remain appropriate for the group.

commonErrors.error: The conceding team stops after the score.
commonErrors.correction: Treat the next defensive action as immediate continuation.

commonErrors.error: The entering team crowds the new football.
commonErrors.correction: Establish width before the restart.

commonErrors.error: Players rush disposals under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten rounds and reinforce controlled first possession.

commonErrors.error: Exiting players interfere with the next wave.
commonErrors.correction: Clear directly through the end line.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase wide runners and leave the corridor open.
commonErrors.correction: Protect central space before matching outside movement.

progressions: Add a second entry football selected by the coach.
Award bonus points for scoring within eight seconds.
Require the entering team to complete a switch before scoring.
regressions: Allow five seconds before the new wave enters.
successIndicators: Sustain purposeful movement across repeated waves.
matchApplication: The game recreates repeated transition phases where players must move from attack to defence or defence to attack without a prolonged stoppage.

title: Movement and Support Assessment Game
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply movement, support and receiving principles introduced across SG-021 to SG-029 during continuous small-sided play.
setup:
Create a directional field divided into three lanes.
Add two movement gates in the middle third.
Mark scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare assessment categories for movement after disposal, support angles, running leads, use of numerical advantage, inside-outside balance and transition.
Conduct four progressive rounds.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one is unrestricted directional play.
Round two awards a bonus for successful overlap or give-and-go movement.
Round three begins each possession with a central ground ball and requires an inside-outside release.
Round four introduces changing numbers through player entry and exit.
A normal scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A score following overlap, third-player movement or a switch-and-surge earns an additional point.
The coach records individual and team movement behaviours.
Teams receive one minute between rounds to identify one movement improvement.
The final round is played without coach intervention.
coachingPoints: Move immediately after disposal.
Create options at different angles and depths.
Use overlap and third-player run when they create advantage.
Maintain width around contested possession.
Lead into the ball carrier’s vision.
Move the football quickly after a switch.
Identify changing numbers.
Transition immediately when possession changes.
Retain support behind attacking movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Whether support options are separated and visible.
Whether third-player movement begins early.
Whether moving targets receive disposals to advantage.
Whether inside and outside players maintain balance.
Whether teams recognise numerical changes.
Whether forward movement continues after switches.
Whether defensive transition remains organised.

commonErrors.error: Players become stationary after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Award assessment points only when movement continues.

commonErrors.error: Support players enter the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Create options at different widths and depths.

commonErrors.error: Movement occurs too late.
commonErrors.correction: Begin running while the previous disposal is travelling.

commonErrors.error: The team forces overlap or return disposals.
commonErrors.correction: Use movement only when it creates genuine advantage.

commonErrors.error: Outside width disappears around contests.
commonErrors.correction: Assign players to remain available outside congestion.

commonErrors.error: Transition slows under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce round duration and reinforce immediate role change.

progressions: Rotate player numbers without verbal warning.
Remove all lane and gate markers.
regressions: Assess only two movement categories per round.
Reduce the number of active players.
successIndicators: Create useful overlap and third-player options.
Sustain team shape during continuous movement.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the movement behaviours required to support possession, break defensive lines, connect teammates and maintain structure during changing phases of Australian football.

title: Decoy Lead Rotation Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to use purposeful decoy leads to move defenders and create space for a second attacking option.
setup:
Create a directional field with an eight-metre scoring zone at each end.
Place two lead-start markers near each attacking scoring zone.
Divide players into two teams.
Each attacking passage must include one decoy lead and one secondary lead before a scoring-zone entry.
Defenders play live and may track, transfer or hold their position.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins near the centre of the field.
As the football approaches the attacking half, one forward makes a strong decoy lead away from the preferred scoring space.
A second attacker delays, then leads into the space created by the decoy.
The ball carrier may use the secondary lead, retain possession or select another clearly superior option.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns one point.
A score created directly through an effective decoy-and-secondary-lead pattern earns two points.
If the defence wins possession, it immediately attacks the opposite end.
Attackers rotate decoy, secondary-lead and high-support roles after each passage.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
The coach changes the preferred starting side between rounds.
coachingPoints: The decoy lead must be fast and believable.
Clear dangerous space rather than leading into it without purpose.
The secondary leader should delay until the defender reacts to the decoy.
Ball carriers must scan both the decoy and the space created behind it.
Deliver the football to the secondary receiver’s advantage.
Do not force the planned pattern when the defence has not moved.
Defenders should communicate whether to follow, transfer or hold space.
Maintain a high support option if both leads are covered.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the decoy lead genuinely moves a defender.
Whether the secondary leader waits for space to open.
Whether the ball carrier scans beyond the first movement.
Whether the entry disposal favours the receiver.
Whether attackers rotate roles.
Whether defenders communicate responsibility.
Whether the team retains possession when the pattern is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: The decoy lead is slow or unconvincing.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate at full intent and demand defensive attention.

commonErrors.error: The second attacker leads too early.
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the defender commits to the first movement.

commonErrors.error: Both attackers lead into the same space.
commonErrors.correction: Separate the directions and depths of the two leads.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier automatically kicks to the second lead.
commonErrors.correction: Use the pattern only when it creates genuine advantage.

commonErrors.error: Defenders both follow the decoy.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate and retain one defender in dangerous space.

progressions: Add full legal bodywork for suitable players.
Require the decoy and secondary leads to cross.
Award defensive points for correctly transferring opponents.
regressions: Nominate the decoy and secondary leader before each passage.
Allow the coach to cue the second lead.
Begin the football closer to the attacking half.
successIndicators: Create and recognise space behind defensive movement.
Retain possession when the planned option is covered.
matchApplication: The game develops coordinated forward movement used to manipulate defenders, clear dangerous space and create higher-quality forward-entry options.
relatedDrills: SG-030 – Movement and Support Assessment Game

title: Cross-Field Run Exchange
objective: Develop players’ ability to exchange positions across the field without collapsing team width or disrupting possession structure.
setup:
Divide the field into left, central and right lanes.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Players may exchange lanes, but each attacking team must retain at least one player in every lane.
A valid exchange occurs when two teammates cross into each other’s lanes while maintaining forward or supporting movement.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team attacking its nominated end.
Players circulate the football while maintaining three-lane width.
Two off-ball teammates may exchange lanes to disrupt defensive match-ups.
At least one exchange must occur before the team can score.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score created within two disposals of a successful lane exchange earns two points.
Defenders may track opponents or transfer responsibility.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Teams play three-minute rounds.
The coach varies whether exchanges occur ahead of, beside or behind the football.
coachingPoints: Begin the exchange before the current ball carrier is fully pressured.
Cross at different depths to avoid collisions.
Maintain at least one wide option on each side.
Communicate the exchange clearly.
Use the exchange to move defenders, not merely to satisfy the rule.
Ball carriers should scan the space created by the crossing movement.
Defenders must decide whether to track or transfer.
Keep a release player behind the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether exchanges occur early enough to affect defenders.
Whether players avoid crossing into the same space.
Whether team width remains intact.
Whether the ball carrier recognises the new option.
Whether defenders communicate the exchange.
Whether players maintain turnover protection.
Whether the movement creates forward advantage.

commonErrors.error: Both players cross at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger the movement so one player goes ahead and one holds deeper.

commonErrors.error: The exchange removes all width from one side.
commonErrors.correction: Require another teammate to fill the vacated outside lane.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier ignores the movement.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the far side before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Players exchange too late.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement while the previous disposal is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Defenders both follow the same player.
commonErrors.correction: Call the transfer before the crossing point.

progressions: Award defensive points for disrupting an exchange.
Remove lane markers once players understand the pattern.
regressions: Require only one exchange during each possession.
successIndicators: Exchange lanes without losing team shape.
Use the space created by defensive reactions.
Defend exchanges through coordinated tracking or transfer.
matchApplication: The game develops coordinated cross-field movement used to break defensive match-ups, create overlap and open new ball-movement lanes.

title: Forward Handball Chain
objective: Develop players’ ability to use consecutive forward handballs to break pressure while maintaining running support and field position.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark a 15-metre central handball zone.
Divide players into two teams.
Kicking is permitted outside the central zone.
Inside the central zone, the team in possession must use handball.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins outside the central zone.
When the football enters the central zone, the possession team moves it by handball.
Players attempt to create a forward-running handball chain.
A minimum of two handballs must be completed before the football leaves the zone.
Once outside the zone, normal disposal choice resumes.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following three consecutive effective forward handballs earns two points.
Defenders apply controlled pressure and may tackle legally where appropriate.
A turnover changes attacking direction.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Run forward before demanding the football.
Receive on the move rather than flat-footed.
Handball into the receiver’s path.
Draw a defender before releasing.
Maintain width between runners.
Keep one support player behind the chain.
Avoid handballing to a teammate under greater pressure.
Defenders should close space without abandoning the next runner.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players receive while moving.
Whether handballs lead the receiver.
Whether the chain gains ground.
Whether runners maintain separation.
Whether the ball carrier draws pressure.
Whether a rear support option remains.
Whether defenders track the next runner.

commonErrors.error: Players stand and wait for the handball.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the run before calling for possession.

commonErrors.error: Handballs are directed at the receiver’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Place the football into the runner’s forward path.

commonErrors.error: Runners become too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width and staggered depth.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier releases before drawing pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry one or two steps until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: Every player runs ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one player supporting behind the chain.

progressions: Require three handballs before leaving the zone.
Award a bonus for a final kick after the handball chain.
Begin each passage with a pressured ground-ball win.
regressions: Permit one kick inside the central zone.
matchApplication: The game develops forward handball chains used to escape congestion, exploit numerical advantage and accelerate through midfield.

title: Backward Release, Forward Re-entry
objective: Develop players’ ability to use a backward release to escape pressure and then re-enter attack through improved spacing and movement.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark a shallow reset arc behind the middle of each attacking half.
Divide players into two teams.
A team may use a teammate inside the reset arc when forward movement is blocked.
After using the reset, the team must re-enter through a different lane.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams attack their nominated scoring end.
When forward options are closed, the ball carrier may dispose backwards to a teammate inside the reset arc.
The reset receiver scans and redirects possession.
The team must re-enter attack through a lane different from the one used before the reset.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within four disposals of an effective reset earns two points.
Defenders may press the reset after the receiver gains possession.
A turnover changes attacking direction.
Teams may not use the reset arc twice consecutively in the same possession.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Use the backward option only when it improves possession.
The reset player should position early and remain visible.
Spread immediately when the football travels backwards.
Change the point of attack rather than returning to the same congestion.
Keep forward players active during the reset.
The reset receiver should scan before possession arrives.
Defenders should press the reset while protecting forward space.
Re-entry must be quick enough to exploit the shifted defence.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether backward disposal is used appropriately.
Whether the reset player is positioned early.
Whether the team creates width during the reset.
Whether re-entry uses a different lane.
Whether forwards remain active.
Whether defenders adjust without losing depth.
Whether the reset produces genuine forward advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players use the reset when a clear forward option exists.
commonErrors.correction: Scan forward before choosing the backward release.

commonErrors.error: The reset receiver stands directly behind pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally to create a clear sightline.

commonErrors.error: The team returns to the same congested lane.
commonErrors.correction: Re-enter through the opposite or central lane.

commonErrors.error: Forward players stop moving during the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Clear and re-lead as the football changes direction.

commonErrors.error: The reset is too slow.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before receiving and dispose early.

progressions: Remove protection from the reset receiver.
Award defensive points for trapping the reset.
Require the re-entry to include a moving mark.
regressions: Protect the reset receiver for three seconds.
successIndicators: Recognise when forward movement is blocked.
matchApplication: The game develops controlled possession used to escape pressure, switch the football and relaunch an attack rather than forcing play into congestion.

title: Blind-Side Support Game
primarySkill: Supporting from the defender’s blind side
objective: Develop players’ ability to create support options from positions outside a defender’s immediate vision.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Place several movement markers five to eight metres outside the central corridor.
Divide players into two teams.
Bonus points are awarded when a receiver arrives from behind or outside a defender’s visual field.
The movement must remain legal and avoid blocking.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
Off-ball attackers position outside the immediate sightline of their defender.
As the ball carrier scans, the attacker moves into a visible receiving lane.
A completed disposal to a blind-side support runner earns one movement bonus.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following a blind-side support bonus earns two points.
Defenders must scan both the football and their opponent.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Players rotate support and high-forward roles.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Begin outside the defender’s direct vision.
Move late enough to preserve surprise but early enough to be seen by the ball carrier.
Enter a clear disposal lane.
Communicate without revealing movement too early.
The ball carrier should scan beyond the immediate defender.
Avoid running into a teammate’s space.
Defenders must use shoulder checks.
Maintain legal spacing and avoid screening opponents.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers begin from genuine blind-side positions.
Whether movement is timed effectively.
Whether the ball carrier sees the late option.
Whether runners enter clear lanes.
Whether defenders shoulder-check.
Whether movement remains legal and safe.
Whether support is still provided behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The attacker moves too early and becomes visible.
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the defender’s attention shifts to the football.

commonErrors.error: The runner remains hidden from the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Move into a clear sightline before calling.

commonErrors.error: The runner enters occupied space.
commonErrors.correction: Scan teammate positions before moving.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier focuses only on the nearest option.
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the first defender.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch only the football.
commonErrors.correction: Use repeated shoulder checks to locate opponents.

progressions: Award bonus points for blind-side movement into the scoring zone.
Require defenders to nominate responsibility after each passage.
regressions: Allow the coach to cue movement.
Slow the speed of play during the first round.
matchApplication: The game develops deceptive off-ball movement used to create uncontested receivers, support ball carriers and exploit defenders who become focused on the football.

title: Wide-to-Centre Fold Game
primarySkill: Folding from width into central support
objective: Develop players’ ability to begin wide, then fold into central space as the football advances.
setup:
Divide the field into two outside lanes and a central corridor.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
At least one attacker must begin each possession in both outside lanes.
Wide players may fold into the corridor after the football crosses the centre line.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in one team’s defensive half.
The possession team establishes width through the outside lanes.
Once the football crosses the centre line, a wide player may fold into the corridor.
The folding player becomes a central support or forward-entry option.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score involving a wide-to-centre fold earns two points.
Another teammate must replace the vacated outside space.
Defenders decide whether to track the folding runner or protect central space.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Hold width until the football advances.
Fold inside at speed rather than drifting.
Time the movement so the corridor is not crowded.
Replace the vacated outside lane.
The ball carrier should identify the folding runner early.
Do not fold when central space is already occupied.
Defenders should communicate tracking and central protection.
Maintain support behind the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players establish genuine width.
Whether the fold begins at the correct moment.
Whether central space remains usable.
Whether the outside lane is replaced.
Whether the ball carrier sees the runner.
Whether defenders communicate.
Whether the movement creates forward advantage.

commonErrors.error: Wide players move inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the football crosses the centre line.

commonErrors.error: Several players fold into the corridor together.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one primary folding runner.

commonErrors.error: The outside lane remains empty.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate positional replacement.

commonErrors.error: The runner jogs into central space.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate to create separation.

commonErrors.error: Defenders both follow the fold.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one player protecting dangerous central depth.

progressions: Require the folding runner to receive within five seconds.
Add a second fold from the opposite side.
Award defensive points for denying the fold.
matchApplication: The game develops the movement of wing, half-back and high-forward players who begin wide and then enter the corridor to support transition or forward entry.

title: Lead, Clear and Fill Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to lead, clear occupied space and replace teammates so attacking structure remains active.
setup:
Create a directional field with three marked attacking pockets near each scoring end.
Divide players into two teams.
Only one attacker may occupy each pocket at a time.
When a player leads from a pocket, another attacker may fill the vacated space.
Players may not remain stationary inside a pocket for more than three seconds.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins near the centre.
As the football enters the attacking half, players occupy the three attacking pockets.
One attacker leads from a pocket.
If the lead is not used, the player clears away from the scoring zone.
Another attacker fills the vacated pocket.
The process continues until a scoring option is created.
A moving receive inside the scoring zone earns one point.
A score created after a lead-clear-fill sequence earns two points.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Rotate players through pocket and high-support roles.
coachingPoints: Lead with intent and clear fully when not used.
Do not return immediately to the same space.
Fill vacated space after the first player has cleared.
Maintain separation between leads.
Ball carriers should scan each new movement.
High players must remain available as release options.
Defenders should communicate exchanges and protect dangerous space.
Avoid standing inside scoring pockets.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether leads are purposeful.
Whether unused leaders clear space.
Whether teammates fill at the correct time.
Whether multiple attackers occupy the same pocket.
Whether ball carriers scan changing options.
Whether defenders transfer responsibility.
Whether attacking movement remains continuous.

commonErrors.error: Players lead and stop in the same space.
commonErrors.correction: Continue through and clear the area.

commonErrors.error: A replacement enters before the pocket is vacant.
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the first player has cleared.

commonErrors.error: Attackers repeatedly return to the same position.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate into a different pocket or high-support role.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier watches only the first lead.
commonErrors.correction: Rescan after each movement.

commonErrors.error: Defenders lose players during exchanges.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate every lead and replacement.

progressions: Require a double lead before scoring.
Award defensive points for maintaining structure through three rotations.
regressions: Begin closer to the scoring zone.
matchApplication: The game develops continuous forward movement that prevents congestion and keeps scoring space available during repeated forward entries.

title: Running Bounce Corridor Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to carry and bounce the football through central space before releasing to a teammate in advantage.
setup:
Create a directional field with a six-metre central carry corridor.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
A player entering the corridor with possession may carry and bounce the football.
The player must release before leaving the far end of the corridor.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins outside the central corridor.
The possession team attempts to release a runner into the corridor.
The runner carries the football forward and completes at least one legal bounce.
Support players move outside or ahead of the corridor.
The runner releases by handball or kick before leaving the corridor.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following a successful bounce-and-release earns two points.
Defenders may enter the corridor and apply legal pressure.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Enter the corridor with speed and space.
Keep the football controlled during the bounce.
Scan before and after bouncing.
Do not bounce when immediate pressure makes it unsafe.
Support runners should remain outside the carrier’s line.
Draw a defender before releasing.
Defenders should close from an angle.
Maintain a release option behind the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the runner enters with genuine advantage.
Whether the bounce is controlled.
Whether the runner scans.
Whether support players maintain separation.
Whether the release occurs before pressure overwhelms the carrier.
Whether defenders close under control.
Whether the team retains support behind.

commonErrors.error: Players bounce directly into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Scan first and dispose when the corridor is closed.

commonErrors.error: The bounce is too far ahead.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the football within a controllable stride.

commonErrors.error: Support runners enter the carrier’s path.
commonErrors.correction: Use outside and forward angles.

commonErrors.error: The carrier holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Release as the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: Defenders approach front-on at speed.
commonErrors.correction: Close from an angle with balanced final steps.

progressions: Award a bonus for a kick after the carry.
Begin each possession with a turnover.
regressions: Remove the mandatory bounce for younger players.
successIndicators: Recognise when central carrying space is available.
matchApplication: The game develops line-breaking run through the corridor, including controlled bouncing, drawing defenders and releasing teammates into attacking space.

title: End-to-End Running Connection
primarySkill: Sustaining running connection across the ground
objective: Develop players’ ability to maintain connected running support from defensive possession through midfield and into attack.
setup:
Divide the field into defensive, midfield and attacking thirds.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
At least two players from the possession team must be involved in each third before scoring.
Players may move freely between zones.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in one team’s defensive third.
The possession team attempts to connect through midfield and enter the attacking third.
At least two different players must touch the football in each third.
Players who dispose are encouraged to continue running into the next zone.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score involving the same runner in two different zones earns two points.
A turnover immediately changes attacking direction.
The team losing possession must recover through the nearest zone.
Play continues for two- to three-minute high-intensity rounds.
Provide sufficient recovery and modify round length for Over 35 players.
coachingPoints: Run to support the next phase after disposing.
Maintain connection between zones.
Avoid leaving the ball carrier isolated.
Use different depths around the football.
Communicate who is advancing and who is holding.
Preserve one player behind the football.
Transition immediately after turnovers.
Manage effort so disposal quality remains high.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players continue running after disposal.
Whether each zone remains connected.
Whether the ball carrier has forward and release options.
Whether runners manage spacing.
Whether one player remains behind possession.
Whether defensive recovery begins immediately.
Whether fatigue reduces skill quality.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the football leaves their zone.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into the next phase as a support runner.

commonErrors.error: Too many players advance and leave no cover.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one holding player behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The midfield receiver becomes isolated.
commonErrors.correction: Move support from both the previous and next zone.

commonErrors.error: Players run in the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Use staggered widths and depths.

commonErrors.error: Disposal quality collapses under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten rounds and increase recovery.

progressions: Require a switch during the possession.
Apply a ten-second limit through each zone.
Award defensive points for forcing a disconnected possession.
regressions: Reduce the number of required touches.
Allow a protected first possession in each zone.
successIndicators: Retain disposal quality under physical load.
matchApplication: The game develops the sustained running connection required to move the football from defensive 50 through midfield and into a scoring position.

title: Small-Sided Movement Phase Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply the complete movement principles developed across SG-021 to SG-039 during realistic small-sided play.
setup:
Divide the field into three lengthways lanes and three horizontal thirds.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare assessment categories for movement after disposal, overlap, third-player movement, decoy leading, lane exchange, inside-outside balance, line connection and turnover recovery.
Conduct four progressive rounds.
Normal Australian football rules apply subject to the stated constraints.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one is unrestricted directional play and establishes a baseline.
Round two awards one bonus point for effective overlap, third-player movement or lane exchange.
Round three requires each attacking possession to include either a backward reset followed by a new lane entry or an inside-outside release.
Round four removes all movement rules and uses a live scoreboard scenario.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A score directly created by an assessed movement pattern earns one additional point.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without stopping routine play.
Teams receive one minute between rounds to identify one movement adjustment.
The final round is played without coach intervention.
Players complete a brief review identifying the movement pattern they used most effectively.
The coach records priority development areas for the next chapter phase.
coachingPoints: Move immediately after disposal.
Create options at different angles and depths.
Use decoy movement to clear space.
Exchange and replace positions without losing width.
Carry or handball forward when central space is available.
Use backward support when forward movement is blocked.
Connect defensive, midfield and attacking lines.
Retain at least one support option behind possession.
React immediately when possession changes.
Apply movement principles according to the game rather than forcing a rehearsed pattern.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Whether movement creates genuine advantage.
Whether decoy and secondary leads are coordinated.
Whether lane exchanges preserve width.
Whether runners receive at speed.
Whether players recognise when to carry, release or reset.
Whether the team connects all three field zones.
Whether support remains behind the football.
Whether defensive transition is immediate.
Whether players independently adjust movement patterns.

commonErrors.error: Players force movement patterns despite poor options.
commonErrors.correction: Select the movement that matches space, numbers and pressure.

commonErrors.error: Several players move into the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Separate options by width and depth.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after completing one movement action.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into the next phase or replace a teammate.

commonErrors.error: Forward movement leaves no turnover protection.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one support player behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The team loses connection between zones.
commonErrors.correction: Assign clear link and replacement responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Movement quality falls under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce round length while maintaining intensity.

progressions: Use hidden tactical objectives for each team.
Add score-and-time consequences to every turnover.
regressions: Predetermine one movement pattern per round.
successIndicators: Move immediately and purposefully after disposal.
Create overlap, third-player and decoy options.
Exchange and replace positions while retaining team shape.
Carry, handball or reset according to the tactical situation.
Preserve skill execution under pressure and fatigue.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the movement principles required for effective Australian football ball movement, including off-ball running, positional exchange, line breaking, forward connection and defensive recovery.
relatedDrills: SG-030 – Movement and Support Assessment Game
SG-037 – Lead, Clear and Fill Game

title: Pressure Box Exit Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to retain possession inside a confined area and identify the correct moment and method to escape into open space.
groundSize:
Central pressure box: 12 metres by 12 metres
Full playing area: 30 metres long by 22 metres wide
setup:
Mark a central pressure box inside a larger directional playing area.
Create a scoring zone at each end of the full field.
Divide players into two even teams.
Begin each possession with the football inside the pressure box.
Position at least two players from each team inside the box and the remaining players outside it.
Outside players may move around the box but may not enter until the football exits.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football inside the central pressure box.
Players inside the box compete to win and control possession.
The team that wins the football attempts to complete a legal disposal to a teammate outside the box.
The outside receiver may then attack the nominated scoring end.
Once the football leaves the box, all players may enter the full playing area.
A clean scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within four disposals of the pressure-box exit earns two points.
If the opposition intercepts the exit disposal, it attacks the opposite end.
After a score, stoppage or out-of-bounds disposal, players reset inside and outside the box.
Rotate inside and outside roles after every two passages.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with a low and balanced body position.
Protect possession before attempting to dispose.
Identify the open release side before collecting the football.
Outside players must maintain width and remain visible.
Use short handball or controlled kick according to pressure.
Avoid every player collapsing onto the football.
Defenders should pressure the ball carrier while also covering likely exits.
Spread immediately once possession escapes the pressure box.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players protect the football under pressure.
Whether outside support remains available on more than one side.
Whether the first disposal exits congestion.
Whether players force disposals through covered exits.
Whether defenders pressure both the ball carrier and release options.
Whether the attacking team spreads quickly after escaping.
Whether transition begins immediately after an interception.

commonErrors.error: Every player collapses into the box contest.
commonErrors.correction: Keep designated outside players available as release options.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner disposes before securing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Stabilise the body and protect the football before releasing.

commonErrors.error: Outside players stand behind defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally until a clear sightline opens.

commonErrors.error: The exit disposal returns into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Identify and communicate the open side before possession is won.

commonErrors.error: Players relax after escaping the box.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate and create width immediately after release.

progressions: Increase the number of players inside the box.
Introduce full legal tackling for suitable groups.
Apply a three-second disposal limit inside the box.
Award a defensive point for trapping possession inside the box for eight seconds.
Require the exit disposal to be completed by handball.
Start selected passages with an unpredictable bouncing football.
regressions: Add a neutral player inside the box.
Delay defenders for two seconds after possession is won.
Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
Allow outside players to enter after three completed disposals.
successIndicators: Win and protect possession under pressure.
Maintain effective inside and outside balance.
Identify and use an open exit.
matchApplication: The game replicates congested stoppage and ground-ball situations where possession must be secured and released to outside runners before the team can attack effectively.

title: Two-on-Two Contest to Score
objective: Develop players’ ability to win a direct contest, combine with a teammate and convert the possession into a scoring opportunity.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Nominate two active players from each team for each passage.
Position one additional support player from each team outside the immediate contest area.
The coach begins each passage with a ground ball, high ball or bouncing football between the active players.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football into the contest area.
Two players from each team compete to win possession.
The team that wins possession may use its outside support player.
The support player enters once a teammate has clearly controlled the football.
The possession team attacks its nominated scoring zone.
The opposition defends and may win possession at any stage.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed without using the outside support player earns two points.
A defensive turnover allows immediate attack towards the opposite end.
Rotate contest and support roles after each passage.
coachingPoints: Establish body position before reaching for the football.
Keep the feet moving through contact.
Secure possession with two hands when possible.
Support players should move early without entering the initial contest.
Use the support player only when it improves the possession.
The nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
The second defender protects the scoring side or intercept lane.
Maintain legal contact and safe tackling technique.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players establish strong body position.
Whether possession is secured before disposal.
Whether the support player enters at the correct time.
Whether teammates create separation after the contest.
Whether defenders divide pressure and protection roles.
Whether tackling remains legal and controlled.
Whether players transition after possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Players reach for the football without establishing position.
commonErrors.correction: Use the hips and feet to secure space first.

commonErrors.error: Both teammates attack the same side of the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Approach from different angles.

commonErrors.error: The support player enters too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside until possession is controlled.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts a rushed disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession and use the nearby support option.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders chase the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one player to pressure and one to protect the scoring side.

progressions: Start with a high marking contest.
Add a third player to each contest team.
Award bonus points for scoring within six seconds.
Begin passages with players in different body positions.
regressions: Begin with a predictable ground-ball roll.
Use touch-only pressure after possession is won.
Allow support players to begin closer.
Give one team a temporary numerical advantage.
successIndicators: Convert contest wins into forward movement.
matchApplication: The game develops the direct contest skills required at ground balls, stoppages and loose-ball situations where players must win possession and immediately connect with support.

title: Tackle-Count Possession Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to retain possession and execute legally when defenders apply repeated controlled tackling pressure.
setup:
Create a directional playing area with two scoring gates at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Apply controlled legal tackling appropriate to the age and experience of the group.
The coach records each completed tackle that forces the ball carrier to stop, change direction or dispose.
Possession remains live unless the tackle produces a legal turnover or infringement.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
The possession team attempts to move the football through either attacking gate.
Defenders apply controlled tackling pressure.
Each completed tackle adds one to the defensive tackle count.
After three completed tackles in the same possession, the defending team earns one pressure point.
The possession team may continue until it scores or turns the football over.
A disposal completed through a scoring gate earns one point.
A score achieved before the defence records three tackles earns two points.
A legal holding-the-football decision or tackle-generated turnover immediately changes possession.
Teams play ninety-second high-intensity rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan and prepare before receiving.
Protect the football on the side away from pressure.
Dispose before the tackle fully controls the body.
Use footwork and change of direction rather than running directly into contact.
Support players should create short, visible release options.
Tacklers must approach under control and keep contact legal.
The second defender should close the likely disposal option.
Reset team shape immediately after a tackle or turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether ball carriers anticipate contact.
Whether players protect the football correctly.
Whether disposal remains legal under pressure.
Whether support arrives before the tackle.
Whether tacklers maintain safe technique.
Whether defenders recover after completing a tackle.
Whether repeated pressure disrupts possession structure.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers run upright into contact.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the centre of gravity and prepare the body earlier.

commonErrors.error: Players hold the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Identify and use the release option before full tackle control.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Move within an effective short-disposal distance.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers leave their feet or use unsafe technique.
commonErrors.correction: Approach under control and maintain legal body position.

commonErrors.error: Defenders admire the tackle and stop.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately to pressure the next possession.

progressions: Increase the tackle count required for a pressure point.
Introduce full match-like tackling for appropriate groups.
Award two pressure points for a tackle-generated turnover.
Add a scoreboard scenario in the final round.
Require a bounce before scoring through a gate.
regressions: Stop play after each completed tackle.
Allow protected possession after a clean mark.
successIndicators: Release legally before being fully controlled.
matchApplication: The game replicates possession chains where repeated tackling pressure forces players to protect the football, release quickly and maintain support around contact.

title: Chaos Ball Recovery Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to react to unpredictable football movement, secure possession and organise the next phase under pressure.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Place the coach outside the middle of the playing area with several footballs.
The coach may roll, bounce, handball, kick or deflect the football into different spaces.
Players begin spread throughout the field.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases an unpredictable football into the playing area.
Both teams react and compete for possession.
The team that secures the football attacks its nominated scoring end.
The opposition immediately organises pressure and defensive protection.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within five disposals of the coach’s release earns two points.
If the football leaves the area, the coach immediately releases a new football.
The coach may release a second football only after the first passage has clearly ended.
Players reset their spread after each score.
Rotate attacking directions between rounds.
coachingPoints: React to the football’s movement rather than guessing.
Slow the final steps when approaching an awkward bounce.
Keep the body behind the football.
Communicate who is attacking the ball and who is supporting.
Take clean possession when possible.
Use the first disposal to escape immediate pressure.
Defenders should react to both the football and dangerous space.
Spread quickly once possession is controlled.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players adjust their approach to the football’s movement.
Whether teammates communicate contest and support roles.
Whether players keep their feet where possible.
Whether possession is secured rather than knocked forward without purpose.
Whether the first disposal exits pressure.
Whether defenders protect the scoring side.
Whether players react immediately to a new release.

commonErrors.error: Players charge at an unpredictable bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and remain balanced.

commonErrors.error: Several teammates attack the same football.
commonErrors.correction: Call one player in and organise support around them.

commonErrors.error: Players tap the football without a clear purpose.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession unless a controlled knock creates advantage.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal remains inside congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the open release side before collecting.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the football leaves the area.
commonErrors.correction: Expect an immediate new football and reset quickly.

progressions: Release the football near the boundary.
Award defensive points for trapping the ball winner.
Start selected passages with one team outnumbered.
Add wet-weather footballs where conditions and safety permit.
regressions: Begin with one player nominated to attack the football.
successIndicators: Spread or recover defensively after the contest.
matchApplication: The game recreates the unpredictable bounces, spills, deflections and loose footballs that occur throughout Australian football and require immediate technical and tactical adjustment.

title: Intercept Reward Game
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to position for intercept possession and convert the turnover into immediate attacking advantage.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
Normal possession and scoring rules apply.
Intercepts are rewarded separately from forced errors.
An intercept must involve a defender cleanly marking, collecting or receiving an opposition disposal.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession and attacks its scoring end.
Defenders pressure the ball carrier and position to close likely disposal lanes.
A clean intercept earns one defensive point.
The intercepting team immediately attacks the opposite end.

primarySkill: Directing possession into a defensive trap
