setup:
Create a directional field with one trap zone along each boundary.
Mark a central corridor.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Before each passage, the defending team secretly nominates one boundary trap zone.
The possession team does not know which side has been selected.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins inside its defensive half.
The defending team applies pressure designed to influence play towards its nominated trap zone.
The nearest defender controls the ball carrier’s inside exit.
Supporting defenders close forward, backward and corridor options.
If possession enters the nominated trap zone and the defence creates a turnover, it earns two defensive points.
A turnover outside the trap zone earns one defensive point.
The possession team earns one point for reaching its attacking scoring zone.
Following a turnover, the defending team immediately attacks the opposite end.
Teams review whether the trap was created through pressure or accidental ball movement.
Roles alternate after each three-minute round.
coachingPoints: Establish the trap through body angle and team positioning.
Protect the corridor before forcing play wide.
Do not reveal the trap by moving too early.
The nearest defender must pressure under control.
Supporting defenders close likely release options.
Retain one defender behind the press.
The possession team should identify when options are being deliberately removed.
Use backward or opposite-side support to escape the trap.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the press influences rather than merely follows possession.
Whether defenders use coordinated angles.
Whether the corridor remains protected.
Whether the nominated trap is concealed.
Whether the possession team recognises the pressure pattern.
Whether an escape option remains behind the football.
Whether turnovers lead to immediate attack.

commonErrors.error: The nearest defender pressures directly and allows an inside escape.
commonErrors.correction: Approach from inside and angle play towards the trap.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders arrive too early and reveal the trap.
commonErrors.correction: Hold shape until the ball carrier commits.

commonErrors.error: The press leaves no protection behind.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one deeper defender.

commonErrors.error: The possession team continues into obvious congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Reset and change the point of attack.

commonErrors.error: Defenders celebrate entry into the trap before winning possession.
commonErrors.correction: Continue pressure until the turnover is secured.

progressions: Allow the defending captain to change the trap during play.
Require the turnover to produce a score for full defensive points.
regressions: Announce the nominated trap zone to both teams.
Reduce the number of pressing defenders.
Pause after possession enters the trap.
Begin with the football closer to the trap side.
successIndicators: Create turnovers inside the nominated trap.
Recognise and escape defensive pressure when in possession.
matchApplication: The game develops advanced team-defence methods used to force opponents towards the boundary, create predictable disposals and generate intercept or tackle opportunities.
relatedDrills: SG-047 – Repeat Pressure and Recover Game

title: Contest-to-Spread Countdown
primarySkill: Spreading rapidly after a contest win
objective: Develop players’ ability to convert a congested possession win into organised width and forward movement within a limited time.
setup:
Mark a central contest zone.
Place one spread gate in each outside lane.
Mark scoring zones at both ends.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin each possession with a contest inside the central zone.
Once possession is clearly won, the coach begins a six-second countdown.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases a football into the contest zone.
Players compete for possession.
Once a team clearly wins the football, the six-second countdown begins.
The possession team attempts to move the football through either outside spread gate.
After passing through a gate, normal directional play continues.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following a successful spread within six seconds earns two points.
The defending team earns one point if it traps possession inside the contest area beyond the countdown.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Rotate starting contest and outside roles after each passage.
coachingPoints: Outside players must begin spreading before possession is fully secured.
The ball winner should identify the open side early.
Use a short release disposal to exit congestion.
Maintain width on both sides until the direction is clear.
Avoid sending every player forward.
Defenders should pressure the first disposal and close spread gates.
Communicate the countdown and release direction.
Continue forward support after exiting the gate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether outside players move before the contest is resolved.
Whether the first disposal exits pressure.
Whether both spread gates remain available.
Whether the ball winner scans early.
Whether defenders close release lanes.
Whether the team continues attacking after spreading.
Whether players retain balance behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Outside players wait for possession to be won.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement as the contest develops.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal remains in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest clear outside support.

commonErrors.error: Every attacker spreads to the same side.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain options on both sides until the release is selected.

commonErrors.error: Players rush and lose disposal quality.
commonErrors.correction: Use the shortest effective release rather than the fastest possible action.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all attack the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Retain players to close outside gates.

progressions: Reduce the countdown to four seconds.
Require the first outside receiver to dispose within two seconds.
Remove one gate after possession is won.
Award defensive points for intercepting the release.
regressions: Extend the countdown to eight seconds.
Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
Allow protected possession for the first outside receiver.
successIndicators: Spread before possession is fully secured.
Preserve disposal quality under time pressure.
matchApplication: The game develops the rapid spread required after winning stoppages, ground balls and congested contests before the opposition can rebuild its defensive shape.
relatedDrills: SG-050 – Pressure and Contest Fundamentals Assessment

title: Pressure Transfer Game
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to transfer pressure responsibility smoothly as the football moves between opponents.
setup:
Divide the field into three lengthways channels.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Defenders begin matched to an opponent but may transfer responsibility as the football moves.
The defensive team earns pressure-transfer points for coordinated exchanges.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession and attacks its nominated end.
The nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
When the football is disposed, the next appropriate defender takes over pressure.
The previous pressure player recovers into support or protection.
Three clean pressure transfers earn one defensive point.
A turnover created after three transfers earns an additional point.
The possession team scores through a receive inside the attacking scoring zone.
A turnover reverses attacking direction.
The coach resets the pressure-transfer count after each turnover or score.
Teams alternate defensive emphasis between rounds.
coachingPoints: Communicate the pressure transfer before the football arrives.
The next defender should move while the disposal is travelling.
The previous pressure player must recover rather than stop.
Avoid two defenders attacking the same ball carrier.
Maintain central and deep protection.
Use body angle to influence the next disposal.
Possession players should move the football quickly to disrupt transfers.
Defenders must remain balanced and avoid overcommitting.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the next defender moves early.
Whether responsibility is communicated.
Whether the previous defender recovers.
Whether duplicate pressure leaves an opponent free.
Whether central protection remains.
Whether the possession team can exploit slow transfers.
Whether pressure remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Two defenders pressure the same player.
commonErrors.correction: Call the transfer early and release the previous defender.

commonErrors.error: The previous defender stops after the disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Recover into the next support or protection role.

commonErrors.error: The next defender reacts after the receiver gains possession.
commonErrors.correction: Move while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Defenders transfer opponents without communication.
commonErrors.correction: Use clear names and directional calls.

commonErrors.error: The defensive line becomes flat.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain staggered depth behind the pressure.

progressions: Require four transfers for a defensive point.
Award bonus points for a transfer-generated intercept.
regressions: Reduce the number of active players.
Count two transfers as one point.
successIndicators: Adjust when the football moves quickly.
matchApplication: The game develops coordinated team pressure where defenders repeatedly hand responsibility to teammates as possession moves across the ground.
relatedDrills: SG-047 – Repeat Pressure and Recover Game

title: Fatigue Decision Contest
primarySkill: Maintaining decision quality under fatigue and pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to preserve sound technical and tactical decisions during repeated high-intensity contest efforts.
setup:
Create a directional field with a central contest zone and scoring zones at both ends.
Divide players into two teams.
Prepare several footballs for rapid restarts.
Play short, intense rounds containing repeated contest starts.
Establish clear workload limits and recovery periods.
Modify volume and contact for younger, returning or Over 35 players.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases a football into the central contest zone.
Teams compete and play continuously towards their scoring end.
When a score, turnover stoppage or out-of-bounds disposal occurs, the coach immediately introduces a new football.
The new football may enter from a different location or direction.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within five disposals of a contest win earns two points.
A poor unforced disposal under fatigue results in immediate opposition possession.
Each high-intensity round lasts sixty to ninety seconds.
Teams receive structured recovery between rounds.
The coach records decision quality, disposal efficiency and defensive reaction.
The final round includes a live score-and-time scenario.
Stop the drill if technique, safety or decision quality deteriorates excessively.
coachingPoints: Maintain composure despite physical fatigue.
Use the first effective option rather than forcing a difficult disposal.
Protect possession before accelerating.
Communicate clearly even when tired.
Recover defensively immediately after turnovers.
Preserve team width and support.
Avoid reckless contact or low-percentage efforts.
Coaches must prioritise quality over exhaustion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether disposal quality declines.
Whether players continue scanning.
Whether communication remains active.
Whether turnover reaction slows.
Whether players force unnecessary contests.
Whether team shape collapses.
Whether contact technique remains safe.
Whether workload remains appropriate for the group.

commonErrors.error: Players rush every disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the decision and use the first effective option.

commonErrors.error: Team shape collapses around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain outside support and defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: Players stop communicating.
commonErrors.correction: Assign clear leadership calls during fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Defensive recovery becomes a jog.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the round so high-quality reaction can be maintained.

commonErrors.error: Contact technique deteriorates.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the passage and reduce load or contact.

commonErrors.error: Players treat exhaustion as the objective.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that the goal is quality decision making under realistic fatigue.

progressions: Introduce full match-like contact for suitable groups.
Increase the number of immediate restarts.
Require a minimum number of different scorers.
Remove verbal coach cues during the final round.
regressions: Reduce field size only if it does not increase unsafe contact.
Reduce total repetitions for Over 35 players.
matchApplication: The game recreates late-quarter and repeat-contest phases where players must continue making effective decisions despite high physical and mental load.
relatedDrills: SG-047 – Repeat Pressure and Recover Game
SG-050 – Pressure and Contest Fundamentals Assessment

title: Small-Sided Pressure Phase Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply the complete pressure-and-contest principles developed across SG-041 to SG-059 during realistic and demanding small-sided play.
setup:
Create a directional field with a central pressure box.
Mark one boundary trap zone and two outside release gates.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare assessment categories covering contested possession, release support, pressing, intercept positioning, repeat pressure, aerial organisation, pressure transfer and decision making under fatigue.
Conduct four progressive assessment rounds.
Adjust contact and workload to suit age, experience and player condition.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one begins each possession with a contested football inside the central pressure box.
Round two begins with a high aerial ball and rewards organised marking, spoiling and ground-level recovery.
Round three uses continuous play with defensive points for intercepts, smothers, trap-zone turnovers and connected pressure transfers.
Round four removes all starting constraints and introduces a live score-and-time scenario.
A scoring-zone receive earns one attacking point.
A score completed within five disposals of a contest or turnover win earns two points.
A clean intercept, legal smother recovery or trap-zone turnover earns one defensive point.
Three connected pressure transfers earn one defensive point.
Teams receive one minute between rounds to review one pressure or contest priority.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without unnecessary stoppages.
The final round is played without coach instruction.
The assessment ends if fatigue causes unsafe contact or unacceptable skill deterioration.
coachingPoints: Establish body position before contesting.
Protect possession when outnumbered.
Maintain inside and outside balance.
Spread rapidly after a contest win.
Apply coordinated pressure rather than individual chasing.
Protect the corridor and dangerous scoring space.
Transfer defensive responsibility early.
Recover after tackles, smothers and corrals.
Organise aerial and ground-level roles.
Preserve decision quality under fatigue.
Transition immediately after turnovers.
Maintain legal and controlled contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players establish effective contest position.
Whether outnumbered players protect and delay.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether teams spread after winning possession.
Whether defensive pressure remains connected.
Whether corridor and scoring-zone protection are maintained.
Whether pressure responsibility transfers smoothly.
Whether smothers and tackles are safe.
Whether aerial and ground-level players organise correctly.
Whether skill and decision quality remain under fatigue.
Whether players transition immediately.
Whether teams adjust independently between rounds.

commonErrors.error: Too many players collapse into the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Retain outside support and defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: Pressure becomes individual and disconnected.
commonErrors.correction: Assign pressure, support and protection roles.

commonErrors.error: Players chase turnovers and leave dangerous space.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the scoring side before attacking the football.

commonErrors.error: Defensive transfers occur too late.
commonErrors.correction: Move and communicate while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner rushes the release disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the first effective option.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes unsafe contact or poor technique.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce load, shorten rounds or stop the assessment.

progressions: Introduce full match-like contact for appropriate groups.
Add late-game scoreboard and time pressure.
regressions: Reduce round length and total workload.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the pressure, contest, defensive trap, aerial recovery and fatigue-management behaviours required during demanding phases of Australian football.
relatedDrills: SG-047 – Repeat Pressure and Recover Game
SG-050 – Pressure and Contest Fundamentals Assessment

title: Kick-Mark Chain Through the Thirds
objective: Develop players’ ability to connect controlled kick-mark possessions through defensive, midfield and attacking thirds without losing team shape.
setup:
Divide the field into defensive, midfield and attacking thirds.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
At least one player from each team begins in every third.
A team must complete at least one marked kick in each third before scoring.
Players may move freely between thirds provided team connection is maintained.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in its defensive third.
The possession team attempts to complete a marked kick before moving into the midfield third.
The same requirement applies in midfield before entering the attacking third.
Players may handball to escape pressure, but only marked kicks satisfy the zone requirement.
A marked kick received inside the attacking scoring zone earns one point.
A score completed without the football returning to a previous third earns two points.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Defenders may apply controlled pressure and attempt to intercept.
Teams play three-minute rounds.
Change starting possession and attacking direction between rounds.
coachingPoints: Create a clear lead before demanding the football.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage side.
Maintain width across each third.
Provide a release option behind the ball carrier.
Move immediately after disposal.
Avoid every player advancing ahead of the football.
The next line should begin moving before the football arrives.
Defenders should protect central lanes while pressuring likely receivers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain connection across the three thirds.
Whether leads begin before the ball carrier is fully pressured.
Whether kicks favour the receiver.
Whether support remains behind the football.
Whether the team becomes too narrow.
Whether defenders protect central space.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.

commonErrors.error: Players stand inside the next third waiting for possession.
commonErrors.correction: Lead dynamically as the previous disposal is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Kicks are directed directly at defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Place the football to the receiver’s advantage side.

commonErrors.error: Every player moves ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one release player behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes narrow through midfield.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain an option in both outside lanes.

commonErrors.error: Players force a marked kick under heavy pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use a short handball or reset before attempting the next connection.

progressions: Reduce the width of each third.
Require two marked kicks in the midfield third.
Award defensive points for intercepts between thirds.
regressions: Add a neutral player in midfield.
Allow a clean kick receive without a completed mark.
Protect the first possession in each third.
Reduce the requirement to two connected thirds.
successIndicators: Preserve width, depth and rear support.
Progress possession without unnecessary backward movement.
matchApplication: The game develops controlled kick-mark movement from defensive 50 through midfield and into attack while preserving team structure.

title: Handball Release to Kick Connection
primarySkill: Linking handball release with kick-mark possession
objective: Develop players’ ability to use handball to escape immediate pressure before connecting with a controlled forward kick.
setup:
Create a directional field with a ten-metre central release zone.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
When possession is won inside the release zone, the first disposal must be a handball.
The next effective disposal must be a kick.
Outside the release zone, normal disposal choice applies.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts each possession with a loose football or short disposal inside the central release zone.
The team winning possession uses handball to release the football from pressure.
The next receiver attempts to complete a forward kick to a moving teammate.
Once the kick is completed, play continues normally.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed through a clean handball-release-to-mark sequence earns two points.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Defenders may pressure the release and close the kick receiver.
Players rotate through inside, release and forward-link roles.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Protect the football before the release handball.
Outside runners must move before the contest is won.
Handball into the receiver’s path.
The release player should scan before receiving.
Balance quickly before kicking.
Forward targets must lead into visible space.
Do not force the kick if the receiver remains under pressure.
Defenders should pressure the release while protecting the next kick option.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial handball exits pressure.
Whether outside support moves early.
Whether the release player scans before receiving.
Whether the kick is balanced and purposeful.
Whether forward targets time their leads.
Whether defenders connect pressure across both disposals.
Whether teams retain structure after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: The release handball goes to a stationary player.
commonErrors.correction: The outside receiver must move before possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: The kicker disposes while off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Take enough steps to stabilise before kicking.

commonErrors.error: The next lead starts too early.
commonErrors.correction: Lead as the release handball reaches the outside player.

commonErrors.error: Players force the kick into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until a clear target appears.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after pressure on the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer pressure immediately to the release player.

progressions: Apply a two-second limit to the release player.
Require the kick to travel at least 15 metres.
Award defensive points for intercepting the first kick.
Begin with uneven numbers inside the release zone.
Remove the compulsory disposal sequence during the final round.
regressions: Protect the release receiver for two seconds.
Allow either the first or second disposal to be a handball.
Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
matchApplication: The game develops the common match sequence of winning possession inside congestion, releasing by handball and then connecting through a controlled kick.
relatedDrills: SG-061 – Kick-Mark Chain Through the Thirds

title: Corridor Draw and Wing Release
primarySkill: Drawing pressure centrally before releasing wide
objective: Develop players’ ability to attract defenders towards the corridor before releasing possession to open wing space.
setup:
Divide the field into a central corridor and two outside wing lanes.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
A possession must enter the corridor before a wing-release bonus can be earned.
Players may use any legal disposal.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in its defensive half.
The possession team attempts to use a central option and draw defensive pressure inward.
Once the football has entered the corridor, the team may release to either wing lane.
A receive in the opposite wing lane earns one movement bonus.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within three disposals of a wing release earns two points.
Defenders attempt to protect the corridor while recovering towards the wings.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Teams play three-minute rounds.
The coach reviews whether the corridor possession genuinely shifted the defence.
coachingPoints: Use central possession only when the receiver can protect or move the football.
Maintain wide players on both sides.
Far-side players must move before the release begins.
Change the point of attack quickly once defenders compress centrally.
Avoid holding the football until the wing advantage disappears.
Maintain support behind the corridor receiver.
Defenders should compress without completely abandoning width.
Transition immediately if the corridor possession is intercepted.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the central possession attracts defenders.
Whether wing players maintain width.
Whether the release occurs quickly.
Whether the far-side receiver moves early.
Whether support remains behind the football.
Whether defenders balance central and wide protection.
Whether teams force dangerous corridor use unnecessarily.

commonErrors.error: The corridor is entered despite heavy pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use central possession only when it can be protected.

commonErrors.error: Wing players move inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until defenders compress.

commonErrors.error: The release occurs after the defence has recovered.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before receiving and move the football immediately.

commonErrors.error: Every player moves ahead of the corridor receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one player behind as a release option.

commonErrors.error: Defenders completely abandon the wing.
commonErrors.correction: Compress centrally while retaining outside awareness.

progressions: Require a kick to complete the wing release.
Award defensive points for intercepting the corridor possession.
Remove one wing lane during selected passages.
regressions: Allow the wing-release bonus without using the opposite side.
successIndicators: Release quickly to open wing space.
Adjust when the corridor is unavailable.
matchApplication: The game develops the ability to use the corridor to compress a defensive structure before switching towards open wing space.
relatedDrills: SG-061 – Kick-Mark Chain Through the Thirds

title: Defensive 50 Exit Grid
objective: Develop players’ ability to exit defensive 50 through coordinated movement, controlled possession and recognition of the opposition press.
groundSize: Half-ground width and approximately 55 metres long
setup:
Use a half-ground area extending from the goal line to approximately the centre.
Place one exit gate in the corridor and one in each outside lane near the end of the area.
Divide players into an exit team and a pressing team.
Begin each possession from a kick-in or controlled defensive possession.
The pressing team scores by winning possession and using a nearby turnover scoring zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The exit team begins with the football at the kick-in starting area.
Players organise short, medium and long options.
The exit team attempts to move the football through any exit gate.
A clean exit through a gate earns one point.
An exit through the corridor earns two points when the option is genuinely open.
If the press wins possession, it immediately attacks the turnover scoring zone.
A turnover score earns two pressing points.
The exit team may switch, reset or use a long contest.
Roles change after four to six possessions.
The coach records exit method, turnover location and decision quality.
coachingPoints: Create width before the kick-in begins.
Provide options at different depths.
Move to create a clear kicking lane rather than standing behind defenders.
Scan the corridor before automatically using the boundary.
Switch early when the press overloads one side.
Retain protection behind risky central disposals.
Pressing players should protect dangerous exits while applying pressure.
After a turnover, defenders must react immediately to protect the scoring zone.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the exit team establishes width and depth.
Whether receivers create clear sightlines.
Whether the ball carrier identifies the press structure.
Whether the switch occurs before pressure becomes fixed.
Whether central exits are selected appropriately.
Whether the pressing team remains connected.
Whether turnover defence is immediate.

commonErrors.error: All receivers lead to the same side and depth.
commonErrors.correction: Create short, medium and long options across the width.

commonErrors.error: The kick-in player holds the football without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Assess the press before the restart and identify the first two options.

commonErrors.error: The team forces a corridor exit.
commonErrors.correction: Use the corridor only when support and space are available.

commonErrors.error: Switch options appear too late.
commonErrors.correction: Far-side players must move before the ball side becomes trapped.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after an exit turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Immediately protect the central scoring area.

progressions: Allow the press to change structure between possessions.
Add a second turnover scoring zone.
Begin selected possessions after a behind with no coach reset.
regressions: Allow the coach to identify the likely open side.
Begin play outside the goal square rather than from a kick-in.
successIndicators: Create visible options at different depths.
matchApplication: The game directly replicates structured kick-ins and defensive 50 exits against an organised opposition press.
relatedDrills: SG-061 – Kick-Mark Chain Through the Thirds

title: Midfield Link to Forward Entry
primarySkill: Connecting midfield possession to forward entry
objective: Develop players’ ability to use a midfield link player to connect possession cleanly with an organised forward entry.

Create a directional field with a midfield link zone approximately ten metres deep.

Play begins in one team’s defensive half.
The possession team attempts to find a moving receiver inside the midfield link zone.
The link player may dispose immediately, carry or reset possession.
Forward players time their movement from the link player’s body position.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark completed within two disposals of the midfield link earns two points.
Defenders attempt to deny the link zone and protect forward space.
A turnover immediately reverses the attacking direction.
Players rotate through link, outside-support and forward roles.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: The link player should move into the zone rather than wait inside it.
Provide more than one link option.
The receiver should scan before gaining possession.
Forward leads must begin when the link player is balanced and able to dispose.
Maintain width around the link zone.
Retain a release option behind the football.
Defenders should pressure the link without abandoning deep protection.
Avoid forcing possession through a heavily defended link zone.

Whether link players arrive with timing.
Whether multiple options exist.
Whether forward leads respond to the link player.
Whether the entry disposal favours the receiver.
Whether outside width remains.
Whether defenders pressure the link and protect depth.
Whether the team resets when the link is closed.

commonErrors.correction: Enter the zone as the football approaches.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead before the link player is ready.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement when the receiver gains balance and vision.

commonErrors.error: Every player moves centrally.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain wide support outside the link zone.

commonErrors.error: The link player turns into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before receiving and use the release option if required.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces a crowded link.
commonErrors.correction: Switch or reset until a clearer option appears.

Add a neutral defender inside the scoring zone.
Award defensive points for intercepting link-to-forward disposals.
regressions: Protect the link receiver for two seconds.

matchApplication: The game develops midfield connection into forward entry, particularly through high half-forwards, wings and central midfield link players.
relatedDrills: SG-061 – Kick-Mark Chain Through the Thirds

title: Retain, Switch and Penetrate
primarySkill: Changing the point of attack before penetrating forward
objective: Develop players’ ability to retain possession, shift the defensive structure and then attack through newly created space.
setup:
Divide the field into three lengthways lanes.
Place two penetration gates between the midfield and attacking thirds.
Mark scoring zones at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
A team must complete possession in at least two lanes before attacking through a penetration gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in one team’s defensive half.
The possession team retains the football and attempts to move the defence laterally.
After using at least two lanes, the team may attack through either penetration gate.
Once the football passes through a gate, the team attacks the scoring zone.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within three disposals of penetration earns two points.
Defenders shift with possession and attempt to close both gates.
A turnover immediately reverses attacking direction.
Teams play three-minute rounds.
The coach removes the lane requirement in the final round to assess natural decision making.
coachingPoints: Retain possession only when it is moving the defence or improving structure.
Switch before the ball side becomes trapped.
Far-side players must move early.
Attack forward decisively when a penetration gate opens.
Maintain support behind the penetrating disposal.
Do not use every lane mechanically if the forward path is already available.
Defenders should shift as a connected unit.
Protect against the reverse switch.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether possession retention has tactical purpose.
Whether the switch moves the defensive structure.
Whether far-side players move before receiving.
Whether the team recognises the moment to penetrate.
Whether rear support remains.
Whether defenders shift without losing balance.
Whether players continue switching when forward space is already open.

commonErrors.error: Teams retain possession without moving the defence.

Whether the highest-value zone is attacked intelligently.
Whether lower-value possession moves defenders.
Whether receivers time zone entries.
Whether defenders reprioritise when values change.
Whether teams become predictable.

commonErrors.error: Players force every possession into the highest-value zone.
commonErrors.correction: Use the best available option relative to pressure.

commonErrors.error: Other scoring zones are ignored.

title: Player-Coached Tactical Adjustment Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify a tactical problem, propose a practical adjustment and apply it without direct coach instruction.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin live small-sided play.
The coach observes without providing tactical instructions.
After a three- to four-minute round, teams receive ninety seconds for player-led review.
Players identify the main tactical problem.
Leaders propose one or two practical adjustments.
The next round begins with the adjustment applied.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score created through the identified adjustment earns one bonus point.
The coach may change the opposition problem between rounds.
Leadership roles rotate during the session.
The final round is played without a formal review break.
Players complete a short post-game explanation of the changes made.
coachingPoints: Identify the problem before suggesting a solution.
Use observable evidence rather than general statements.
Limit each review to one or two changes.
Include players from different field positions.
Leaders should organise rather than dominate.
Adjust spacing, numbers, tempo or role responsibility according to the problem.
Evaluate whether the change improved performance.
The coach should guide through questions only when required.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify the actual tactical issue.
Whether proposed solutions are practical.
Whether several players contribute.
Whether leaders communicate clearly.
Whether the adjustment is applied during play.
Whether performance improves.
Whether teams abandon the adjustment too quickly.
Whether players independently modify the plan when conditions change.

commonErrors.error: Reviews focus only on skill errors.
commonErrors.correction: Include spacing, numbers, structure and decision making.

commonErrors.error: Players suggest too many changes.
commonErrors.correction: Select one priority adjustment.

commonErrors.error: One leader controls the discussion.
commonErrors.correction: Require input from different positions.

commonErrors.error: The adjustment is not applied after the restart.
commonErrors.correction: Assign responsibility to specific players.

commonErrors.error: Teams persist with an ineffective change.
commonErrors.correction: Review the evidence and modify the plan.

progressions: Give both teams hidden tactical objectives.
Require teams to adjust without speaking to the coach.
Record the game for player-led video review.
regressions: Provide a list of possible tactical problems.
Allow the coach to ask guiding questions.
matchApplication: The game develops on-field leadership and collective problem solving required when players must adjust tactics between goals, at quarter breaks or during changing match conditions.

title: Advanced Constraint and Decision Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to process changing constraints, recognise tactical problems and select effective solutions during advanced small-sided play.

Create a directional field with one end scoring zone at each end.
Add two side scoring gates on each side.
Divide the field into three lengthways lanes.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare assessment categories covering scanning, target recognition, objective selection, numerical advantage, press recognition, scoreboard management, communication and leadership.
Prepare constraint cards that may alter scoring targets, player numbers, defensive structure, disposal time or scoreboard conditions.
Conduct four progressive rounds.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one uses changing active scoring gates and rotating zone values.
Round two introduces changing player numbers through delayed entry and recovery.
Round three gives the defending team a hidden press and gives both teams competing tactical objectives.
Round four uses a live scoreboard scenario and player-led tactical adjustments.
A scoring-zone receive earns the value assigned to that target.
A score completed through an identified numerical or structural advantage earns one bonus point.
A turnover in a high-risk area gives the opposition one transition bonus.
The coach changes selected constraints during live play.
Teams receive ninety seconds between rounds for player-led review.
The coach records decision quality rather than only successful execution.
The final eight-minute block is played without coach instruction.
Players complete a post-assessment tactical review.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving and while the football is moving.
Understand the current scoring, number and time conditions.
Identify what the opposition is attempting to remove.
Select the option that balances value and risk.
Use numerical advantage before it disappears.
Retain possession when the high-value route is closed.
Adjust tempo according to the scoreboard.
Communicate changes immediately.
Maintain rear-side protection.
Use player leadership to solve emerging tactical problems.
Avoid forcing rehearsed patterns that do not match the game.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan for changing information.
Whether teams understand current scoring values.
Whether numerical advantages are identified.
Whether players recognise hidden defensive structures.
Whether possession decisions match risk.
Whether tempo reflects score and time.
Whether rear-side protection remains.
Whether communication reaches all lines.
Whether players lead tactical reviews.
Whether adjustments improve performance.
Whether decision quality remains under pressure and fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players focus on one constraint and ignore others.

commonErrors.error: Tactical reviews contain too many adjustments.
commonErrors.correction: Select one or two priority changes.

commonErrors.error: Rear-side protection disappears during aggressive attack.
commonErrors.correction: Retain at least one player behind the football.

progressions: Remove all visual scoring and zone markers.
Introduce full match-like contact for suitable groups.
Assess players by positional and leadership role.
Allow players to design the final constraint set.

Display all scoring and time information clearly.
successIndicators: Balance tactical value against turnover risk.
Operate independently of constant coach instruction.

title: Six-Six-Six Restart Game
primarySkill: Restart structure and first-phase ball movement
objective: Develop players’ ability to organise quickly after a goal, win or defend the first possession and connect the restart with purposeful attacking movement.
setup:
Create a reduced oval-shaped playing area with a central square.
Mark one forward starting zone and one defensive starting zone for each team.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin with equal numbers positioned in midfield, attack and defence.
Adjust numbers proportionally when fewer than 18 players are available.
Each passage begins with a coach-controlled ball-up or neutral release inside the centre square.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in their nominated restart positions.
The coach releases the football inside the centre square.
Midfield players compete for first possession.
Players outside the centre square may enter once the football is clearly touched or controlled.
The team winning possession attacks its nominated scoring end.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within six disposals of the restart earns two points.
If the defending team wins possession, it counterattacks immediately.
Following every score, players must return to their restart positions within twenty seconds.
The coach varies the restart location and ball flight.
Teams may make one structural adjustment between rounds.
Play continues for three- to four-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Arrive at restart positions quickly.
Establish clear attacking, defensive and outlet roles.
Midfielders must communicate who is attacking the football and who is protecting the exit.
Outside players should hold their starting width until the football is released.
Forwards should separate rather than all leading towards the same space.
Defenders must protect the dangerous side of the restart.
The first disposal should move the football away from congestion.
Players must transition immediately when the opposition wins the clearance.
Avoid overcommitting every player to the centre-square contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players return to restart positions quickly.
Whether midfield roles are clear.
Whether outside players maintain useful spacing.
Whether the first disposal exits congestion.
Whether forwards create separate options.
Whether defenders protect the scoring side.
Whether both teams transition immediately after the clearance.
Whether players adjust their structure between rounds.

commonErrors.error: Players arrive late to starting positions.
commonErrors.correction: Use a countdown and restart regardless of readiness.

commonErrors.error: Every midfielder attacks the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign first possession, support and defensive-cover roles.

commonErrors.error: Outside players collapse into the centre square early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the football is released.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal returns into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the open side before the ball-up.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into the same area.
commonErrors.correction: Establish different depths and directions before the restart.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch the clearance and lose opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Protect dangerous space while tracking forward movement.

progressions: Reduce the time allowed to reset after a score.
Award bonus points for a centre clearance followed by a moving mark.
Allow teams to change restart structure without coach notice.
regressions: Use a controlled coach handball instead of a ball-up.
Reduce the number of active forwards and defenders.
Stop after the clearance to review positioning.
successIndicators: Connect the clearance with forward movement.
matchApplication: The game replicates post-goal centre restarts and develops the organisation required to win the clearance, defend the opposition’s first possession and connect quickly with attacking targets.

title: Clearance to End-Zone Conversion
primarySkill: Converting stoppage possession into a scoring opportunity
objective: Develop players’ ability to turn a stoppage win into an organised scoring opportunity before the opposition can restore defensive structure.
setup:
Mark three possible stoppage-start circles through the middle third.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Position inside midfielders, outside players, forwards and defenders.
Each passage begins with a ball-up, boundary-style release or ground-ball stoppage.
The team winning the clearance has ten seconds to attempt a scoring-zone entry.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach selects one stoppage circle and releases the football.
Players compete for possession.
The winning team attempts to release the football to an outside player or forward-facing midfielder.
The ten-second conversion count begins once possession is clearly controlled.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone within ten seconds earns two points.
The defending team earns one point if it delays the attack beyond ten seconds.
If the defending team wins possession, it counterattacks towards the opposite end.
A score after an opposition stoppage win earns two counterattack points.
Rotate stoppage and outside roles after each passage.
Vary the start location and defensive setup.
Play continues for repeated passages.
coachingPoints: Win the football with a clear release plan.
Outside players must move before possession is secured.
The first receiver should face or move towards the attacking end.
Use handball to escape immediate pressure.
Forward players should create width and separate their leads.
Avoid rushing a low-percentage kick solely because of the countdown.
Defenders should pressure the clearance source and protect central space.
If the fast conversion is unavailable, retain possession rather than concede an easy turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the stoppage win has an intended release.
Whether outside players hold useful width.
Whether the first receiver can face forward.
Whether forward movement begins early.
Whether the countdown creates poor decision making.
Whether defenders delay and protect dangerous space.
Whether teams retain possession when immediate conversion is unavailable.
Whether counterattack begins immediately after a defensive win.

commonErrors.error: The clearance is won without outside support.
commonErrors.correction: Position release players before the stoppage begins.

commonErrors.error: The first receiver faces backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Move into a forward-facing position before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Every forward leads towards the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Separate by width, depth and direction.

commonErrors.error: Players force a scoring entry because of the countdown.
commonErrors.correction: Use the first effective option, not the first possible option.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all attack the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Retain central and deep protection.

regressions: Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
Stop after the first disposal for positional review.
successIndicators: Win possession with a release option.
Defend the clearance as a unit.
Retain possession when the fast score is unavailable.
matchApplication: The game develops conversion from centre and around-ground stoppages into forward entries before the opposition can reset behind the football.
relatedDrills: SG-065 – Midfield Link to Forward Entry

title: Red-Time Possession Game
primarySkill: Controlling possession late in a quarter
objective: Develop players’ ability to protect a narrow lead during the final minutes of a quarter without becoming passive or predictable.

Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
One team begins with a lead of one to seven points.
Set the clock between sixty seconds and three minutes.
The leading team begins with possession in a nominated area.
The trailing team must regain possession and score before time expires.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, time and starting possession.
The clock begins when the football is released.
The leading team attempts to maintain safe, purposeful possession.
The trailing team applies coordinated pressure and attempts to force a turnover.
A scoring-zone receive earns the predetermined score value.
A marked disposal that clearly retains possession may allow the clock to continue.
Out-of-bounds and infringement rules are applied consistently.
A turnover immediately changes tactical priorities.
When time expires, the scenario ends.
Teams review one successful and one poor decision.
Starting score, time and field position change for the next scenario.
Both teams rotate through leading and trailing roles.
coachingPoints: Know the score and remaining time.
Maintain active movement during controlled possession.
Use width, backward support and the boundary strategically.
Avoid dangerous central turnovers.
Continue taking safe territory when available.

The trailing team should press as a connected unit.
On-field leaders must communicate time and tactical priorities.

Whether players know the score and time.
Whether controlled possession remains active.

Whether communication remains continuous.
Whether tactical behaviour changes immediately after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: The leading team becomes stationary.

title: Two-Minute Defensive Hold
primarySkill: Defending a narrow lead under sustained pressure

Use a half-ground area with one attacking scoring zone.
Place two defensive exit gates near the opposite boundary.
Divide players into an attacking team and a defending team.
The defending team begins with a narrow scoreboard lead.
Set a two-minute countdown.
The attacking team receives repeated possession after scores, out-of-bounds footballs or coach-directed restarts.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score and remaining time.
The attacking team begins with possession outside the scoring area.
The defending team attempts to protect its lead for two minutes.
A scoring-zone mark earns the attacking team the nominated score.
If the defence wins possession, it attempts to exit through either gate.
A clean defensive exit removes ten seconds from the clock and restarts the attack.
An intercept mark removes fifteen seconds.
If the attack scores, the scoreboard is updated immediately.
The defence must reset quickly after every passage.
The scenario ends when time expires or the attacking team takes the lead.
Teams reverse roles after each scenario.
The coach varies starting position and score margin.
coachingPoints: Protect central and deep scoring space first.
The nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders close the most dangerous options.
Do not concede uncontested short possessions that improve entry angle.

Avoid unnecessary infringements that stop the clock or concede territory.
Maintain composure through repeated entries.

The coach announces the score and remaining time.
The trailing team attacks immediately.

After any score, the coach quickly restarts play from the centre or a nominated location.
If the leading team wins possession, it may retain the football or counterattack.
The trailing team applies immediate pressure after every turnover.

title: Small-Sided Games Chapter Final Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to independently apply the technical, tactical, physical and behavioural principles developed throughout the complete Small-Sided Games chapter.
groundSize:
Junior or foundation groups: 35–50 metres long and 25–35 metres wide
Advanced groups: 65–85 metres long and 42–52 metres wide
howTheDrillWorks:
Phase one begins as unrestricted directional small-sided play.
Phase two introduces a contested restart and rewards effective clearance conversion.
Phase three introduces a hidden defensive press or temporary numerical imbalance.
Phase four uses a scoreboard and time scenario.
Phase five becomes a coachless match simulation.
A normal scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A score created through a recognised tactical advantage earns one additional point.
A defensive intercept, tackle-generated turnover or coordinated pressure sequence earns one defensive point.
Teams receive brief player-led reviews between the first four phases.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without unnecessarily stopping play.
The final phase is played without tactical coach instruction.
Players conduct the first post-assessment review.
The coach records chapter-level strengths, priority improvements and suitable future progressions.
